tieu_de: What Causes What Effect
tom_tat: People in this world encounter all kinds of strange things, why? That's because people previously planted a strange cause, so now strange results are born. If you don't sow that kind of seed, you won't reap that kind of seed...
noi_dung:
What Causes What Effect

People in this world encounter all kinds of strange things, why? That's because people previously planted a strange cause, so now strange results are born. If you don't sow that kind of seed, you won't reap this kind of fruit. Therefore, if everyone understands the principle of Cause and Effect, then:

Evil deeds,

They serve well.

(Do not do evil,

Only do good deeds.)

In this world, people cannot separate from Cause and Effect; However, because everyone only sees the effect and not the cause, when the retribution comes, they are frantic and confused, not knowing what to do right! That's all because when growing seeds, people didn't know how to be careful, waiting until they had to receive strange retributions, then they were startled and shocked!

We are currently studying the Four Kinds of Purity and Repentance (Four Commandments About Purity) in the Shurangama Sutra. This Sutra Text explains very thoroughly the complex and strange Cause and Effect cases of humans. If you want to clearly understand the issue of Cause and Effect, "don't do evil, only do good." Every day, you should not only think about your personal gain but find ways to bring benefits to others; However, there is no need to boast: "I often do many things that benefit others! I repair pagodas, give alms, help the poor..." Such things are not for boasting or talking

empty, but needs to be truly practiced. Take helping people as a source of joy and consider it your vocation; If so, this world will naturally become better!

(Lectured on April 30, 1983)

"Taking Fake as Real"

Confucius said:

The taste of filial piety is like false filial piety.

(I have never seen anyone who loves virtue as much as they love beauty !)

At that time, Confucius realized that people who love morality and conduct are not as focused as people who love beauty, so he sighed and lamented: "I have never met anyone who admires morality as much as he admires beauty!"

I have never seen anyone who loves Buddha Dharma and works so hard that he loves money! You see, no matter how much people love Buddha Dharma, there are times when they feel tired. When they bow to Buddha, chant sutras or chant mantras for a long time, they feel tired. However, if you go out to make money, even if you don't eat, drink, or sleep, you won't feel tired! Just look at those who love gambling and know that they don't rest all day and all night, but their eyes are still dry and not tired at all!

How can humans be like that! That's because people don't perceive things clearly; On the contrary, when it comes to fake things, they " rush after them like ducks, " pursue and search frantically, it's absolutely crazy!

(Evening sermon April 30, 1983)

tieu_de: Immersed in the Classical Meaning
tom_tat: If you want to study Buddhism, you need to clearly understand the meaning in the sutras. Each sutra preached by the Buddha contains a distinct true meaning; However, all scriptures are interrelated and…
noi_dung:
Understanding the Meaning of the Classics

If you want to study Buddhism, you need to clearly understand the meaning in the sutras. Each sutra preached by the Buddha contains a distinct true meaning; However, all scriptures are interrelated and their meanings are also interrelated.

The Buddha cited the Hinayana, the Mahayana, and finally converged on a single vehicle, the Buddha Vehicle. Regardless of whether it is Mahayana, Hinayana, or Buddha, yana teaches people to correct bad habits, eliminate ignorance, wipe out afflictions and eliminate greed, anger, and ignorance. If you can get rid of all bad habits, there will be a natural compatibility with the meaning of the scriptures; If you do not give up bad habits, you will not be able to fully grasp the meaning in the sutra.

We are studying Shurangama Sutra, and have now finished studying the Fifty Skandhas (Fifty Skandhas) and the Four Purity and Repentance (Four Commandments About Pure Nature). So, what is the true meaning of this sutra? Why did the Buddha preach this sutra? Only when you find it can you be considered to truly understand the teachings contained in the sutra; If you cannot find the true meaning, it will be considered that you have not truly understood the Dharma! For example, you meet someone, even though you know that person's name, you still need to "go one step further", clearly recognize that person's appearance, thoughts, behavior, etc.; That's how to recognize that person. If you only know the person's name but know nothing about the person's appearance, thoughts..., then that is still not awareness. It's the same when we study Buddhist scriptures!

The form of Shurangama Sutra is "the big child has no outside, the small child has no inside." (so big that nothing can go beyond it, so small that nothing can be smaller than it). Nghĩa lý của Kinh Lăng Nghiêm ví như bộ xương người vậy, nếu con người không có xương, chỉ có da, thịt, gân, máu... mà thôi, thì chẳng ra hình dáng con người cũng chẳng thể nào đứng vững được. Therefore, The Shurangama Sutra is the essence of the sutras. Kinh Lăng Nghiêm có công dụng "phá tà hiển chánh" - phá hủy tất cả tà vạy để hiển lộ Tam-muội chân chánh. If there is no Shurangama Sutra, there is no Buddha Dharma; There is The Shurangama Sutra, there is Buddha Dharma! So, if we want to protect the Buddha Dharma, we must first propagate and disseminate Language Sutra Seriously - we must learn it by heart, explain it well, and then practice accordingly.

The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is "Surangama Arhat" - Bodhimanda of Shurangama Sutra. We must definitely shine "Surangama Great Light," practice "Surangama Great Concentration,"achieve "Surangama Great Wisdom" and reach perfection "Surangama Great Compassion!"

(Lectured on May 1, 1983)

tieu_de: Making a Wish Must Come From a Sincere Heart
tom_tat: Practitioners need to make vows with the most sincere heart and must always follow the vows they have made, otherwise, after making the vow within five minutes, they will completely forget it, because then...
noi_dung:
Vow Making Must Come From Sincerity

Practitioners need to make vows with the most sincere heart and must always follow the vows they have made. Otherwise, after making a vow in less than five minutes, they will completely forget it, because then it is as if they had never made a vow at all! You need to clearly realize one thing - why do you make a vow?

Making a vow does not depend on formality; Therefore, if you consider making a vow as a ritual that must be followed according to the rules, then you are completely wrong and have gone against the principle of making a vow. Those who have made a vow should recite their vow text once a day to remind themselves and motivate themselves to try to fulfill it to the utmost perfection; That way you won't disappoint your original intention of making a vow.

The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, thanks to having seriously made their vows and practiced them according to their vows, attained Supreme Enlightenment. Therefore, if we continue to carry out each of our vows in a truthful way, without any deception, we will also become Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! The Buddha is a man of great wisdom, and we are a man of great ignorance; Therefore, if we want to learn according to wisdom, we must take the Buddha's mind as our mind, take the Buddha's vow as our vow, always be compassionate and joyful, endure things that others cannot endure, and complete things that others cannot do. Everything must be done honestly in order to achieve true response. Therefore, everyone must pay special attention to making vows!

Amitabha Buddha, by making forty-eight vows, achieved the World of Ultimate Bliss and guided all Sentient Beings. We should learn from the behavior of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Saints of the past, must earnestly correct previous mistakes, should not hide our shortcomings, and should not indulge in our bad habits - this is called "enlightenment" (turning our backs on the world, returning to enlightenment); If on the contrary, it is "enlightenment in harmony with the world" (turning away from enlightenment to harmonize with the world).

If you can boldly correct your mistakes, face reality, accept challenges, and then overcome all difficult challenges, then you will have the opportunity to achieve success. Don't have self view too deep, self view too heavy. You need to know that self nature is inherently upright and pure, and is called the true mind "complete, bright, straightforward, not attached to anything even as small as a thread." This true mind has no bad habits or defects at all; Therefore, do not entrust Buddha-nature to the material created by the four great elements.

Why do we "abandon the truth and follow the false?"Why do we "abandon the roots and find the top?" It is because we do not recognize our own self nature! Self nature is pure, without any contamination, and is like a bright mirror. "Hybrid objects block light, past objects blocks purity" (when an object arrives, the mirror immediately reflects the shadow of the object, when the object leaves, the mirror is as clear as before, without traces).

You! A person who cultivates the Way but cannot correct his mistakes is the same as not cultivating. There is a saying:

Fifteen years of action, four decades of nine years of action.

(Only at the age of fifty did I realize the mistakes of forty-nine years ago.)

Anyone who has such an enlightened mind must be a wise person; That person's future path will certainly be vast and spacious, it can be said that "progress is as brilliant as brocade." If you don't know your own mistakes, you will be confused for the rest of your life, only knowing " vain names," being confused by other people - people like that are so pitiful!

Currently, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a Bodhimanda that radiates light to all places and is protected by tens of thousands of Buddhas. Hopefully everyone can dispel the darkness in their minds; However, you need to apply wisdom illumination to illuminate your mind in order to wipe out all ignorance and afflictions. You must be very careful and pay special attention to this point!

tieu_de: The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas - A Fairy Scene Between Human World
tom_tat: The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a quiet, solitary place. Here, the air is fresh and the scenery is elegant, there is no air pollution and no noisy traffic noise. Pham is someone who lives on the campus of…
noi_dung:
Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas - Fairy Scenes Between Human World

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a quiet, solitary place. Here, the air is fresh and the scenery is elegant, there is no air pollution and no noisy traffic noise. Everyone who lives on the campus of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must appreciate and wholeheartedly preserve and protect the environment.

In the Dai Tung Thu pine forest on the Thanh Thanh campus, there are several hundred white cranes that nest in trees and live there all year round. This bird belongs to the species posterbird, and should be able to migrate to other places depending on the climate, but these white cranes keep "stationed" here forever, refusing to "move house", enough to see how fresh the air in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is!

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is also a Holy Land, with more than thirty sika deer (apricot blossoms) living on the vast grassland; They walked leisurely in the steppe and whenever they saw someone coming, they jumped up and happily greeted them. Baby deer are even more endearing. They cling to their guests and refuse to leave.

In the Holy City there are also weasels and foxes, but they do not harm small animals. If they break the Precepts - even if they eat a small squirrel - they will still be punished by the Guardian God. These ferrets are very mischievous. If someone sees them and stomps their feet, they imitate and stomp their feet. If they roll their eyes at them, they also stare back! The little weasel is very innocent, whenever he meets a monk he follows him. Sometimes they even enter the house or loiter in front of the door to ask for food.

All the birds bathed in this sacred, magical, pure and serene fairyland all live in harmony and peace; It can be said that they have found the right environment!

tieu_de: In all things, patience is precious
tom_tat: The secret of practitioners is to eat less. Why? Because eating less causes less sexual thoughts. If you meditate less, you can know what is enough (satisfaction). If you know enough, you will always be at peace. Always peaceful, there is no affliction. No worries…
noi_dung:
All Things, Patience is Precious

The secret of practitioners is to eat less. Why? Because eating less causes less sexual thoughts. If you meditate less, you can know what is enough (satisfaction). If you know enough, you will always be at peace. Always peaceful, there is no affliction. Without afflictions, Bodhi arises. When Bodhi arises, you will be liberated. Achieving liberation means being able to "free destiny, free birth and death, free wisdom"- in short, completely free. Those are the stages that practitioners must go through; Everyone, let's try together!

Cultivators need to be patient. No matter what challenging situation comes to them, they must use patience to endure, grit their teeth and endure; Once you have passed "the gate", then "the wind will calm down and " will naturally be at peace. When working, if there are things you don't want to do, you should be patient and do them. Over time, you'll get used to it and it will become natural. In short, no matter what job we do, we should do it properly and conscientiously; Don't be lazy, avoid work for leisure, or do it carelessly to get things done. If you have the idea of ​​" being a Venerable for one day then ringing the bell for one day, " is contrary to the Tao; This class of people is just " relying on Buddha for clothing, relying on Buddha to earn food, " living day by day, certainly without any prospects!

I use the two words "patience" as the motto for my life - no matter the situation, I definitely refuse to give up, resolutely endure everything with both my body and mind. When I was still in my hometown in the Northeast, I was used to "bear heat and cold." On days "tam nine"2 (the coldest period of the year), I didn't wear shoes or socks at all, just walked barefoot in the freezing cold weather, causing my feet to freeze to the point of pain - but I still tried to endure, as long as I was patient, I no longer felt the pain! During the few days of "tammu"3 (the hottest period of the year), the weather was so hot that it made my head dizzy and my face dizzy; As I walked, I kept seeing darkness in front of my eyes, as if the sky and earth were spinning upside down. Many people feel so hot that they feel weak, but I find that it's not too bad, just sit and rest for a while and you'll be fine. I take the two words "patience" as Dharma treasures to overcome all difficulties - to endure cold and heat, to endure the rain and to endure the sun, to fast and to endure thirst; I patiently endured everything, determined not to "pull the white flag" to surrender.

After becoming a monk, I focused on practicing the Dharma of Patience. What if someone scolds me? Then I just pretended like I didn't hear anything, or I thought I was listening to music, and suddenly I was safe and sound! What if someone hits me? I absolutely do not fight back, but only accept with a calm and peaceful attitude! I also patiently practiced the Late Night Kung Fu and Evening Kung Fu rituals - early in the morning. When it was almost time to go to the Main Hall, even though I was sleeping soundly, I immediately woke up when I heard the sound of the gong signaling me. I rinsed my mouth and washed my face, and after getting ready, I went up to the main hall to wait; I always arrive five minutes early, never once have I been late!

Since becoming a monk until now, I have always used patience to work. When I go to other places to research and learn, whether it is to perform the Late Night Gong Phu, the Evening Gong Phu, to preach the Sutra and preach the Dharma, to listen to the Sutra and listen to the Dharma, or to make offerings at noon, I always arrive earlier than the scheduled time, and have never been a bit late! Today I bring my past story to tell you, that is, "incarnately preaches Dharma"!

If you want to practice correctly, you must not be lazy. When working, you must be positive, enthusiastic, and not lack patience. Even if there are things you cannot endure, you must endure them, and if there are things you cannot endure, you must endure them. Patience and enduring everything - that is the guideline of a practitioner. Especially while you are still learning and practicing, you must try to be more patient and tolerant; Even if you really can't bear it anymore, you still have to try your best to endure! There is a sentence:

Ren and engraving, peace and tranquility,

The most rotten, the sea is completely empty.

(Be patient, the wind is calm,

Take a step back, the sea is wide and the sky is high.)

You must not arbitrarily lose your temper; must know that:

Ignorance's fire energy destroys merit! (The fire of ignorance can burn down the forest of merit!)

That is a very reasonable quote and also an experienced observation. Everyone, remember this and keep it in your heart! Be careful, don't get angry!

You should not arbitrarily get angry, thinking that this is not right, that this is not right, or that whatever you see makes you feel uncomfortable or uncomfortable. It is true that in life there are many things that do not go as you want, but please "take a step back" and remind yourself: "You must be patient! We have to be patient!" If we can be patient, everything will be fine, all the troubles and troubles will no longer exist!

We, as practitioners, need to do all work properly and thoughtfully, not be lazy, not careless, or careless. Everyone must strictly follow the rules of Bodhimanda; Don't say: "Every day I come to listen to the Sutra lectures, I'm never absent, so other things just go by the wayside, just in general!" This thought is truly unacceptable! Whether it's Midday Worship, Late Night Kung Fu, Evening Kung Fu or Dharma Assembly, you should come to the Main Hall a little early to wait for the ceremony time, because then the retribution that will come to you in the future will be complete. Otherwise, if you are late for every class, you may later miss the opportunity for enlightenment. If you are late in doing anything, your merit will not be complete.

We, practitioners, should not reason with ourselves or act as our own lawyers. There should be a saying:

Like a visionary, like a visionary.

(What goes around comes around.)

Whenever you plant good deeds, you will reap good results, if you sow evil deeds, you will reap evil rewards - that is the law of "heavenly scriptures and earthly meanings, " is the eternal law of heaven and earth. If you plant a complete seed, when it bears fruit, you will get a complete fruit. If you plant a half-baked or incomplete seed, you will produce a half-baked or incomplete seed. Everyone needs to really understand this point, and not be indifferent, just like the wind blowing in their ears!

(Lectured on May 1, 1983)

Living in the Ashram Must "Depends on Us"

Bodhimanda's rule is that if there is work, everyone does it together. When we eat, we eat together, when we do meritorious deeds, we do it together. However, there are still exceptions, for example, people who really know how to meditate and meditate every day can do less other work. Why? Because they use effort like that, it means they have practiced! And reciting Buddha's name or bowing to Buddha are both practices. If there is such a special situation, then it is an isolated case and we do not need to mention it. If you are not in a special case, you absolutely must not be lazy or skip work to stay healthy, but must simultaneously follow the rules and regulations of Bodhimanda.

You don't always sit in Zen, nor do you always bow to the Buddha, but when you do the Late Night Gong Fu and Evening Gong Fu ceremonies, you don't have time to participate (but you have time to talk nonsense), or it's already time to do the Late Night Gong Fu and Evening Gong Fu ceremonies and you keep procrastinating. You're late, I'm late, and everyone else is late too, so who should we let do the Late Night Gong Fu and Evening Gong Fu sessions? What does a practitioner do if he does not perform the Late Night Kung Fu and Evening Kung Fu ceremonies?

In Bodhimanda, the Late Night Kung Fu and Evening Kung Fu sessions are the common work of Thuong Tru, a job that no one can avoid. Not doing the Late Night and Evening Kung Fu ceremonies means looking down on Bodhimanda, but looking down on Bodhimanda means looking down on Buddha, and looking down on Buddha is like looking down on the masses. If you look down on the masses, " cannot coexist, " cannot live together; And that means we can no longer practice together with everyone!

Except for the time to practice the Late Night Kung Fu and Evening Kung Fu, the remaining time is up to each person to do whatever they want. Whoever wants to translate the sutras will translate the sutras, whoever wants to read Buddhist books will read Buddhist books, whoever wants to talk nonsense will go talk nonsense, whoever wants to listen to gossip can just listen to gossip, no one will interfere or stop you. However, when it is time to perform the Late Night Kung Fu and Evening Kung Fu ceremonies, you must definitely participate, because the Late Night Kung Fu and Evening Kung Fu ceremonies are an indispensable method, a mandatory course of Bodhimanda.

People who practice the Way need to protect, preserve and respect Bodhimanda, and must follow all regulations of Bodhimanda. Whenever you hear the bell and drum ringing signaling that the ceremony time is approaching, everyone must immediately drop all unfinished work to prepare to go to the Main Hall, without delay. Everyone needs to have the spirit of "competing for the future", always trying to get ahead, not being left behind. If you think that the Late Night Kung Fu and Evening Kung Fu sessions are not important and only reluctantly participate, then you are truly in Bodhimanda waiting to go to hell! There is a sentence:

The gate of hell before the Sangha.

(In front of the gates of hell, there are many teachers and Taoists.)

Regardless of whether you are a monk or a lay person, once you have lived in Bodhimanda, you must know how to rejoice in your merits and seriously do Buddhist work; You can't follow or follow others, because then there's really no prospect!

tieu_de: Affliction is Bodhi
tom_tat: The Buddha saw that Sentient Beings endured four great sufferings: birth, old age, illness, and death, so he decided to become a monk and practice, looking for a way to solve that problem. In our ignorance, afflictions suddenly appear - sometimes...
noi_dung:
Defilement is Bodhi

The Buddha saw that Sentient Beings endured four great sufferings: birth, old age, illness, and death, so he decided to become a monk and practice, looking for a way to solve that problem. In our ignorance, afflictions suddenly appear - sometimes manifesting through physical appearance, sometimes latent in the mind, and sometimes ignorance arises so we don't know anything. As soon as ignorance acts, we immediately become confused, so afflictions are the cause and condition that hinder cultivating the Way, and are obstacles on the path of the Way.

However, it is impossible not to have troubles! Why? Because " affliction is Bodhi." If you know how to use it, affliction is Bodhi. If you don't know how to apply Bodhi, it turns into affliction! Bodhi is like water and afflictions are like ice; Water is ice, ice is water. Water and ice are inherently the same thing, not two different things. When it's cold, water freezes into ice, and when it's hot, ice melts into water. So, in other words, when there is affliction, it means "water turns into ice," and when there is no affliction, it means "ice melts into water;" This reason is very easy to understand. Again, if there is affliction, there is "ice" affliction -emptiness minh, and without affliction there is "water" Bodhi -wisdom. Regarding this point, please remember it practically and keep it in your heart! When we cultivate the Way, we should not cultivate for eighty thousand eons and this affliction still exists. Every day "eat" live in sorrow, if you don't "eat" in sorrow, you will starve to death, because that would be very pitiful!

Where do our illnesses come from? It is from the three poisons of greed, anger, and ignorance! If humans did not have these three poisons, there would be no diseases. Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom in Buddhism are the specific remedies to treat the disease "greed, anger, ignorance." This medicine is as effective as a god, "medicine comes, illness goes," should say:

The mind is clear, the water shows the moon,

determined, immeasurable.

(The mind calms down, the water shows the moon,

Stop, the sky is cloudless.)

That is the realm where there are no more afflictions. There is a sentence:

The mind only recites: true wealth, the end of desire: true field of blessings. (The mind stops, thoughts stop: real wealth, all desires are gone, it is a field of blessings.)

The mind's delusions stop completely, the idea of ​​fate is gone, that is true wealth. In short, not being greedy means being rich. Why are people greedy? Because they are not "content,", they feel lacking and incomplete! Not having desires is a field of blessings. If you can get rid of all selfish desires, it is truly a field of blessings. Please pay special attention to:

Peace of mind: all tribulations are dispersed,

concentration: ten thousand things come to an end.

(A calm mind, a hundred misfortunes will disappear,

calm, all things are auspicious.)

The above quote is very reasonable and extremely useful, worthy for everyone to take as a golden rule.

What is "Afflictions"? " is disturbing the body, mind, and mind, " is not peaceful and free.

"What is "? Uu means "sorrowful, " sad, unhappy.

What is "Hanh"? Hoanh means "non calamity, " means calamity, sudden unfortunate occurrence.

These things bind or oppress you, making you feel like you are locked tightly by the "lock of ignorance, " is tied tightly by the rope of afflictions, or feel suffocated like a big rock is pressing on you. It is precisely because he wants all Sentient Beings to get rid of all afflictions to achieve peace and freedom from all oppression to achieve liberation that the Buddha advised all Sentient Beings to develop a broad Bodhi mind and practice the merits and virtues of the Buddha. Therefore, all of us Sentient Beings should obey the Buddha, believe in the Buddha, and follow the teachings even more!

The mental afflictions of Sentient Beings are immeasurable and limitless, but you should know that they are like the illusions seen when blinded by sunlight. Sentient Beings go crazy, turning straight into crooked, crooked into straight; Black becomes white, white becomes black; Taking good for evil, taking evil for good, no matter how we educate, we still have the same defects and obstacles pile up. If their shortcomings are pointed out, not only will they not be happy, refuse to correct their mistakes, and not improve, but they will also find ways to cover up and justify their mistakes, and even become greatly ignorant, giving rise to great afflictions. When Bodhisattvas saw such Sentient Beings, they felt compassion and mercy, wholeheartedly taught them, five times seven times warning them not to talk nonsense, not to give rise to troubles; and also said that if they do not get angry, are not jealous, and do not hinder others, they will overcome the ocean of suffering.

The human body is temporary, don't look at this smelly "leather bag" as a treasure and worry about cherishing and taking care of it, fearing that "it" will be miserable and hard. You want "it" to be happy and at ease, but "it" always causes more trouble and trouble for you!

(Lectured on May 3, 1983)

How To Get Rid Of Afflictions?

The Bodhisattva saw that Sentient Beings in the Three Realms all suffered from the afflictions of the Three Poisons: greed, anger, and ignorance, so they had to endure all kinds of suffering, burning, and constant oppression.

In theory, people who become monks and practice the Way should not have afflictions; However, in reality, many people still have countless afflictions! Why? Because their minds are not pure, they keep seeing that this is not right, that is not right, that this person has mistakes, that person has shortcomings... In short, they are surrounded by many afflictions, causing their body and mind to not be free and peaceful. Think about it, everyone has their own sorrows, from the president to the beggar, everyone has their own sorrows and sufferings! The leaders of countries around the world today are worried about the country's fortunes, tomorrow they are worried about the people. They have many things to worry about and worry about. As for beggars who go out to beg, when they encounter people who don't want to give alms, they can also get angry and get upset. If you want to be free of afflictions, there is only one solution:

Need to practice Precepts, Concentration and Wisdom,

That means destroying Greed, Hatred, and Stupidity.

(Diligence in the Precepts of Concentration,

Abandon Greed, Anger, and Ignorance.)

When practice is complete, afflictions will naturally no longer arise.

It is because of Sentient Beings suffering from the disease "Three Poisons,"disease "defilements" that Bodhisattvas have developed great compassion and popularized antidotes. The Buddha preached eighty-four thousand dharma methods to treat eighty-four thousand afflictions of Sentient Beings, which are eighty-four thousand prescriptions that have the power to soothe and cure all diseases and sufferings of Sentient Beings. However, just studying the prescription without taking the medicine is of no use; Therefore, people who study Buddha Dharma need to have the effort of "faith, understanding, practice, and realization" to be able to achieve it!

Dharma Talk On Buddha Bathing Day

There is disagreement between the Southern and Northern sects about the Buddha's birth date. However, no matter what day it is, as long as everyone respectfully remembers and solemnly worships, that day is the day Buddha was born. Because " has no definite dharma, ", even if you research this issue until your hair is gray and your eyes are blind, you still won't be able to find a correct answer. It's just a waste of precious time. What a pity!

According to Buddhism, every person in general has attachments and attachments. Some people are attached to Indian Buddhism, others are attached to Sri Lankan Buddhism, Chinese Buddhism or Japanese Buddhism, etc. It is because of attachments and differing viewpoints that make Buddhism limited, have boundaries, and cause division within Buddhism.

In fact, Buddhism is limitless and boundless, without a certain scope. Therefore, I have always advocated that we should not draw boundaries for Buddhism, but on the contrary, all must unite and agree, "one world" is correct! I often say: "The Buddhism I preach is not Indian Buddhism, nor is it Chinese Buddhism, but the Buddhism that 'goes to nothingness, transforms the Dharma Realm!'" To be more clear, no Buddhism has a nationality, no Buddhism has a race, and there is also no Buddhism that divides humanity, self, or self! Not only those who believe in Buddhism are disciples of Buddha, but even those who do not believe in Buddhism are disciples of Buddha! Why? Because Buddha Shakyamuni once taught:

Necessarily Sentient Beings,

Buddha nature,

Work with Buddha!

Means:

All Sentient Beings,

All have Buddha nature,

Let's all become Buddhas!

This proves that people who believe in Buddha are Sentient Beings, and people who do not believe in Buddha are also Sentient Beings!

Someone said: "I am not Sentient Beings!" Then, try asking:

"You are not Sentient Beings; Then what are you?"

Some people even assert: "My name is Thien (heaven), then I am heaven!"

You should know that: "Heaven" is also a Sentient Beings!

There are also people who say: "My name is Dia (earth), then I am land!" You should remember that: "Dai" is also Sentient Beings and does not go beyond the circle of Sentient Beings!

The ends of the void and throughout the entire Dharma Realm are the residence of Sentient Beings. Of the ten Dharma Realms, only the Buddha Dharma Realm is beyond the circle of Sentient Beings; Surprisingly, the remaining nine Dharma Realms (Bodhisattva, Pratyekabuddha, Sravaka, Heaven, Human, Asura, Animal, Hungry Ghost, Hell) all belong to the circle of Sentient Beings, so they are all called "Sentient Beings."

We are all Sentient Beings, then, if I consider those who do not believe in Buddhism to also belong to Buddhism, what is unfair? This is the nature " of the entire great use" of Buddhism. Buddha taught:

Most Sentient Beings can become Buddhas!

(All Sentient Beings can become Buddhas!)

Whether you believe in Buddhism or not, in the future, you will all become Buddhas! Why? Because you can't escape the cycle of Sentient Beings! Those who do not believe in Buddha at present will believe in Buddha in the future; This life does not believe in Buddha; then the next life can believe in Buddha, in short, everyone will believe in Buddha, therefore all Sentient Beings are considered disciples of Buddha.

Nowadays, there are religions that do not preach morality, but assert that: "There is only one God, who can rule the world, create the world, and control the universe. Humans are not qualified to be Gods, but can only be slaves to Gods and subject to God's influence!" This type of reasoning is very contrary to the Principles of Buddhism!

According to the Principles of Buddhism, anyone can become a Buddha. The Sentient Beings of the present life are our parents in past lives and Buddhas in the future. If we have anger towards Sentient Beings, it is the same as anger towards our parents and Buddhas; And that means we become ungrateful and rebellious people! Therefore, towards Sentient Beings, we need to be compassionate and respectful. Between people, we should treat each other sincerely and be willing to help each other; Don't be afraid or jealous of each other. That is the greatest point of Buddhism.

Today, if you come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to participate in the Buddha Bathing Ceremony, I consider you as disciples of Buddha (without knowing whether you believe in Buddha or not, whether you bathe Buddha or not!) Those who believe in God are also considered disciples of Buddha, those who believe in Jesus are also considered disciples of Buddha. Even those who believe in Judaism, Islam, etc. I also consider them as disciples of Buddha. I absolutely do not consider you guys as "outsider" to Buddhism. Everyone is one family, in the same family, regardless of one person or another. You see, Buddhism has absolutely no thoughts against other religions, how great it is!

(Lectured on May 9, 1983)

Cause and Effect of Loan Repayment, Not a Little Mistake

After half a year of recuperation, his health recovered; Now I can continue to copy the Avatamsaka Sutra, my wish has been fulfilled. Today I have so many emotions, so I borrowed a pen to write down a few thoughts.

In the spring of 1975, the writer of this article had the good fortune to meet a Supreme Being in Japan and was accepted by him as a disciple. In the fall of that year, this person went to the United States, vowing to dedicate himself to Buddhism and take on the job of copying scriptures. Wishing to repay the Teacher's gratitude, I worked hard and faced the altar

Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva made three great vows: (1) Not to compete for more or less; (2) Do not discuss right or wrong; (3) Don't forget gratitude or resentment. During the recent illness, I changed it to "not remembering gratitude or resentment" (instead of "not forgetting gratitude or resentment") and decided to focus on practicing the Dharma of Patience, no matter what adversity I encounter, I try to hold back my heart and endure it, not trying to avoid it. Why? Because my karma is too heavy, I have to use this method to eliminate it!

People get sick, there's a reason. This writer is very ashamed and willing to accept retribution.

Now I respectfully write down this cause and effect to encourage my friends. I hope that you will have deep faith in the issue of Cause and Effect, be careful when planting the causes, and quickly achieve the results of the Path!

tieu_de: Food for the Spirit
tom_tat: The reason why people fall into hell, become hungry ghosts, or turn into animals is not beyond the influence of the Six Roots. The reason people become A-tu-la, are born in heaven or become human, is not apart from the effect of the six senses...
noi_dung:
Food for the Spirit

The reason why people fall into hell, become hungry ghosts, or turn into animals is not beyond the influence of the Six Roots. The reason people become A-tu-la, are born in heaven or become human, is not apart from the effect of these six senses. Even if a person becomes an Arahant, a Pratyekabuddha, a Bodhisattva or a Buddha, they will not leave the functions of these six senses. Why do these six senses have such great power? Even whether people are born in heaven or fall into hell, they cannot be separated from them? Are these six senses capable of influencing humans in the matter of becoming a Buddha or a demon?

In fact, it's not that these six senses control us, it's that we don't know how to use them. In the self-nature (or enlightened spirit) of every human being, there is an "his owner." This "owner" is also our inherent Buddha nature. When the "owner" is in power (that is, the Buddha nature is present), mindfulness is present, doing everything freely, without obstacles. However, if there is a thought of ignorance or ignorance aroused in our mind, then these six senses will be like six enemies, they will overwhelm the host, they will usurp the power of the "owner" and we will be harmed by the six enemies of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and thoughts. These six robbers will destroy the house and rob it, taking all the precious assets in the house! So say:

One thought without birth is fully manifested,

The six senses were startled and shocked.

(One thought does not arise: Buddha nature appears,

The six senses awaken: the mind is clouded.)

Therefore, we originally followed the Buddha's path but then fell into the demonic path! For example, there is a person driving a car who should have been traveling on a main road but he crashed into the sea, causing both the person and the car to sink to the bottom of the sea; There are people who like far-fetched things. They run up the mountain and then fall from the top of the mountain, causing their body to be broken. That's because they don't know the road, don't know how to walk, don't know how to drive, so unexpected things happen that can even endanger their lives.

The inherent spiritual nature of man is omnipresent, extremely perfect, wonderful, clear, manifests in all ten directions, and has unparalleled power, allowing him to accomplish anything. For example, there is a person who knows how to drive, but once reincarnated in this rotten "leather bag", he becomes very confused, and doesn't even know the direction of east, west, south, north, or up or down anymore, so he keeps running around everywhere. When people are obscured by the six senses, they also want to become Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, but with just a little mistake or lack of care, they can become a horse, a cow, or a goat!

The most pitiful thing is that there are some Buddhist believers who wholeheartedly want to escape the three evil paths,5 but do not understand how to drive this car, do not know how to use the six senses, so they are controlled by the six senses and have to let the devil take control of their "house". They are trapped in this temporary body made up of the five aggregates and cannot escape. Their suffering is unspeakable, their original spiritual nature is lost, and their bright wisdom cannot appear!

Therefore, everything, everything in the world teaches the Dharma, teaches us the truth; If you understand, you will see that all things are preaching Buddha Dharma, speaking the Dharma out of the world; But if you don't understand, you will see that everything is just talking about worldly dharma, contaminated dharma! Therefore, everything depends on your mind, it all depends on your thoughts. As long as you have wisdom, you can solve any problem with ease and freedom; Without wisdom, there are only obstacles everywhere!

Although our human body needs to eat and drink to survive, it is only a rudimentary food. Humans also have to rely on Buddha nature and bright wisdom to survive. For example, a car needs gasoline to run, people also have to rely on food to have vitality, to be able to live, and to be able to move. However, there are some practitioners who do not need to rely on food to survive; Why is that? Because they only "eat" the light of wisdom, that is the real nutrition for them! Therefore, in terms of roughness, the body needs to rely on food and drink; But looking at a more subtle depth, humans need to have Buddha's spiritual nature to be food for the spirit. During the day when we work, whether we walk, stand, lie down or sit, we waste vital energy, just like a car consumes a lot of gasoline. When we rest at night, our pores open and come into contact with the Buddha's aura, absorbing the luminous wisdom radiating from the Buddha's Great Light Treasury to replenish the spirit that was consumed during the day. Therefore, thanks to a full night's rest, the next day the spirit is restored to normal!

Many people hear this principle and immediately become greedy, thinking: "Ah! It turns out that when I sleep, Buddha 'injects' his halo; So if we sleep a little more, wouldn't we be more intelligent?" In fact, each person only needs a certain amount of sleep; If you sleep too much, your mind will be dull and your wisdom will decrease. People often say "da long dream da" (the night is long, there are many dreams); People who dream all the time are just wasting their spirit! Sleeping too much can make us drowsy and have headaches; Therefore, whatever you do must be appropriate and moderate, and should not go to extremes!

People who do not understand this principle think that only eating and drinking can maintain life; However, those who practice the Tao and know how to put effort into it pay great attention to spiritual food, so they love to meditate, study and practice Meditation. Because it is through meditation and concentration that they can come into contact with much of the Buddha's brilliant wisdom to replenish their spirit and cause their wisdom power to grow further. However, when it comes to Zen or meditation, you should not be too greedy, being too attached to meditation can cause "Zen disease!"

Therefore, those of us who study Buddhism should not run to the west or the east, looking outward in pursuit of the Dharma, looking for shortcuts, or being greedy for conveniences, wanting to quickly become enlightened, because that only causes the limited energy level in our bodies to be wasted, ourselves to be exhausted, our wisdom to be reduced, and yet to achieve nothing! That is the bad state of not understanding anything about the principles of " the fundamental Buddha nature, " just turning your mind outward to pursue the Dharma!

What I'm talking about today is not a myth, but can be called "theory!" This theory, it can be said that even the most advanced scientists have not been able to research it, let alone understand it, and even in their wildest dreams they could not dream that there is such a wonderful morality! Actually, these are very normal principles, but unfortunately everyone is indifferent and doesn't pay attention!

(Lectured in May 1983)

tieu_de: Muu Sanh and Muu Tu
tom_tat: You "old youth" and you "young seniors!" Today everyone gathered here, if not for a great fate, then also for a small fate. What I want to say is that no one can deny it
noi_dung:
Mushen and Muzi

(Talking to students from Redwood University at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas,

noon May 21, 1983)

You "old youth" and you "young seniors!" Everyone gathered here today, if not a great fate, then a small fate. What I want to say is that no one can deny it!

Why do I call you "old youth?" Because I see that you young people look very spirited, have a very mature, cautious and mature attitude, so I call you old youth. Why do I call "young seniors" too? Because I see that among you there are many older people who are very open-minded, young, have no calculating mind, no jealousy, no obstacles, no self-centeredness, so I call those people young seniors. Some of you came here last year; Because it's unclear whether the friends coming this year are those people or whether there are both new and old people coming together, so we can both say you are new friends and we can call you old friends!

Our City of Ten Thousand Buddhas has Principles that want to change the atmosphere of education. In the world, the Three Teachings, Nine Streams, 7 Five Classes and Eight Actions 8 have all the professions, everyone makes a living (worries about living) and no one wants to commit suicide (worries about dying)! No one worries about how he will die; If you live, you live, but what happens when you die? Because no one thinks about that problem, I say no one plans to commit suicide. However, in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, there are people who seek life and others who plot death.

Usually people make a living by trading, farming, being an official, working as a worker, studying, etc. People freely choose one of the five professions of scholar, farmer, worker, merchant, and official to do; That's why some people choose a job in education. However, there are many people who want to use students as tools to gain profit, so they calculate: "If I open a school, if people come to study, how much money will I make? With this much money, I can make a living!" Therefore, they use all kinds of methods to make their school the most famous. But when it became known as "supreme school", the school became decadent; Why? I feel very ashamed to have to say things like this: At many schools, students openly buy and sell opium and smoke opium! Do you find that pitiful? There are also people in school who openly do illegal things.

Seeing such a situation, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas established a primary school to teach students how to fulfill filial piety, and a secondary school to teach students loyalty and patriotism. At the same time, we also established a university to teach loyalty, filial piety, benevolence, filial piety to parents, loyalty to the fatherland, and treating society with humanity. That is the Principles, the direction of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. In addition, primary schools, secondary schools and universities in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas are completely free. Why is it free? Because I don't want to take advantage of students for personal calculations and gain. That is the educational style of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

At the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, regardless of whether they are elementary, middle school, or university students, whether they are monastics or lay people, they all follow the following Six Great Principles:

First is No Fighting. I don't compete with you, and you don't compete with me; If people compete with us, we will not compete with others. If we do that, all conflicts in the world will disappear.

Second is Non-Greedy, means that we are not greedy for everything.

The third is No Seeking, means not chasing, not craving for anything.

Fourth is Unselfishness.

Fifth is Non-self-interest, means not scheming for one's own gain; and

The sixth is No False Speech, means not lying.

Those are the Six Great Principles that everyone in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas needs to practice. When you come to visit the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, I do not want to propagate but just want to introduce to you the Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. We hope that young people will make special efforts to help your country and make your nation and people peaceful and happy. Please try to work together!

The Secret to Memorizing the Sutras

One block of light and sound, one block of gold,

Longing for gold and pain, longing for light and sound,

The loss of gold is so convenient,

The light and sound of the past is difficult to find again!

(An inch of time: an inch of gold,

Gold cannot buy an inch of time,

A lost inch of gold is easy to regain,

It's been lost for a while and it's hard to find!)

From morning to night, people compete and strive for nothing more than to earn food, clothing, wealth, shelter and fame. Because of these five things, everyone goes crazy, from dawn to dusk there is no time to rest. Sometimes when they don't have to go to work and are at home, they are busy with all sorts of activities such as watching TV, playing computers, playing stocks, watching movies, traveling, etc.

People in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas are also busy, but that busyness is completely different. Here, no one is busy about food, clothing, or accommodation. It's okay for people in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas not to pay attention to those things; As for fame and fortune, they are even more indifferent. However, everyone is very busy. But why are you busy? Busy studying Buddhism, Dharma, and Sangha; Busy cultivating Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom, the nature is completely different from other people. Here, when we study the scriptures every day, we need to pay special attention, not only that the body is there but the mind is running away, not knowing where to run! You should not think that this person teaches the Dharma well so you should pay attention, while the other person does not preach well so you are absent-minded and do not pay attention. If you keep focusing on cause, self, and right and wrong, your love and hate will be very heavy, your attention to right, wrong, good, and bad will also be very strong, and you will not be able to completely overcome or eliminate it.

When listening to the Sutras, you need to be very sincere and attentive. If people preach well, we should learn and imitate their methods. If people don't preach well, we should pay more attention and listen, using the Wisdom of Wonderful Observation to judge whether their preaching is correct or not, in accordance with the Dharma, with the truth or not; Don't use your conscious mind to differentiate and compare to find mistakes. For every gesture and action of any person, you must pay special attention, pay attention and learn, don't let it go to waste; Only then will you have a place to gain, and you will be able to open up your wisdom. The opening of wisdom cannot be achieved in a day or a night. It requires us to practice like that in the morning, and like that in the afternoon, from morning to night we must continuously study, without interruption; Only then will there be a chance for success.

Now everyone is studying the Shurangama Sutra and Shurangama Mantra. You need to know that the Shurangama Sutra is the true body of the Buddha, and is also the Buddha, the Dharma, the Sangha, the Precepts, the Concentration, and the Hue. If you want to respect the Sangha, you must first respect the Shurangama Sutra. If you want to study Precepts, practice Concentration, and develop Wisdom, you must first study the Shurangama Sutra. There are eighty-four thousand methods of Buddhism, but the Shurangama Sutra is complete, just right, neither redundant nor lacking. We must study this Sutra, and we must learn it by heart and fluently. The learning method is that every day you study a passage of scripture, and every day you have to review the parts you have memorized. Don't be eager to learn a lot, learn quickly, you have to review once a day to be able to memorize it. Once you have mastered and matured, you will become sophisticated and skillful; Only with sophistication is born flexibility and sensitivity. There is a sentence:

Skillful energy gives birth to cleverness, cleverness gives birth to spirit. (Get used to it, become proficient, become flexible.)

It is essential that you never leave what is close and run to look for what is far away, nor do you turn your mind outward to pursue or chase; because it is only a superficial practice, not a method to penetrate the Sutra Pitaka and open wisdom.

What time should we take advantage of to memorize the sutras? In the morning, when you wake up and change clothes, or when you are brushing your teeth and washing your face, these are all times when you can silently recite sutras. At night when you go to bed, even though your head is on the pillow, you can still read quietly. If you can make the effort to study the sutras continuously, without interruption, you can memorize them very quickly.

The method of studying sutras has "three to." The first is "eye to"; second is "mouth to"; and the third is "mind coming." When both eyes, mouth and mind are single-minded, attentive towards the sutra, you will memorize it very easily.

There are also three possible places to memorize the sutras. The first is on the road, the second is on the pillow, the third is at the toilet. These three places are very convenient places for memorizing sutras. If you apply this method, you can memorize the sutras very fluently. Please experiment!

tieu_de: The Taste of True Dharma
tom_tat: The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the Bodhimanda of the Avatamsaka realm, the mandala of the Shurangama Sutra and the Shurangama Mantra, and also the treasure of the Dharma of the Forty-Twelve Eyes. Every day we spend time in this treasure trove studying…
noi_dung:
True Dharma Taste

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the Bodhimanda of the Avatamsaka realm, the mandala of the Shurangama Sutra and the Shurangama Mantra, and also the treasure of the Dharma of the Forty-Twelve Eyes. Every day we spend time in this treasure trove studying morality precisely because we want to get rid of ignorance about enlightenment, reform evil, and eliminate desires and cravings. If you can do so, you will end evil thoughts and break through the membrane of crazy ignorance. At that time, you no longer need to study the Buddha Dharma anymore, because you have left the edge of ignorance to return to enlightenment, left the wrong path to return to the right path, returned to the original source of existence.

However, while you have not reached such a place, have not reformed your evil ways, have not cut off desires and eliminated craving, have not returned to your original nature, and have not yet returned to your origin, you must make every day an effort to study the Mahayana sutras such as the Shurangama Sutra, Avatamsaka Sutra, Lotus Sutra, Six Patriarch Dharma Jewels Sutra, Ksitigarbha Sutra, Diamond Sutra, etc. You need to be dedicated, sincere and earnest in cultivating the truth. You should not just superficially use the effort like " scratching an itch through your shoe, " but need to attain the true taste of the Dharma to have practical use!

(May 27, 1983)

Robbers in the house are difficult to guard against!

From time immemorial until now, the Six Senses of ordinary people keep running after the external environment, that is, Luc Tran9 while " looking for the sharp sword, " creates countless impure karma. Human eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and mind are like six crooks acting as brokers for the enemy, they lead the robbers into the house to take away all the precious property in "house" of our self-nature.

We think of our eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and mind as things that help us; In fact, these six things are six very evil things. They lead crooks into your home to rob you of all the Dharma treasures of your own nature without you even knowing it; Indeed, " robbers in the house are difficult to guard against!" Now let's talk about eyes and ears:

Eyes without prejudice, speech without prejudice,

No ears, no worries.

(Eyes do not see, mouth does not crave,

If the ear does not hear, the heart will not be troubled.)

When we see others eating delicious food, we naturally want to taste it, and then become greedy for food. When we hear good words, we feel happy; When you hear harsh, discordant words, you become angry. Các bạn đừng cho rằng mắt là vật tốt, giúp mình nhìn thấy, bởi vì chính do sự giúp đỡ của mắt mà sanh ra đủ thứ phiền não, như khi mắt nhìn thấy sắc đẹp thì mình sanh lòng tham sắc đẹp, tham tới mức là mình đạt được nó thì lòng sanh phiền não, mà không đạt được nó thì cũng sanh phiền não! Ngay cả mũi, lưỡi, thân, tư tưởng hay ý niệm cũng đều như vậy, chúng khiến mình phát sanh đủ thứ phiền não, mà một khi phiền não nảy sanh là mình mất đi Pháp bảo tự tánh; should say:

The most scorching of the sun and the sun. (A thousand days of chopping wood, one day of burning it all.)

Cũng vậy, mình tu dưỡng công phu Thiền Ðịnh cả ngàn ngày, nhưng đến khi đạt được cảnh giới khinh an tự tại rồi, thì hốt nhiên chỉ vì khởi một niệm phiền não mà bao nhiêu công phu đều tiêu tan cả; should have the sentence:

The fire of the chimpanzees burns away the forest of merit.

(A small spark can burn away an entire forest of merit.)

Therefore, people who practice the Way need to:

The eye contemplates form and form, without internal existence,

The ear hears things, the mind does not know.

(Eyes see shapes, heart does not move,

Listen to the world, it's not good!)

You must have such Concentration in order to avoid people coming to rob your house of precious things. If not, then all day long you will follow the Six Senses and Six Objects, your mind running outward, not knowing how to reflect the light, and that is called "contraband, " means affliction. When you have gonorrhea, you will wander forever in the three evil paths, with no end in sight; Isn't that scary? To eliminate afflictions, we must first find the cause of afflictions. The Buddha taught that the Six Consciousnesses10 are the enemy in the house. Because the Six Roots colluded with the Six Dusts, they were born

Six Consciousnesses, then because of that, "begins delusion, creating karma, " becomes confused, causing all kinds of bad karma. Therefore, the Six Senses are the brokers who lead us to create evil deeds.

"What is the family heirloom" (treasure) in my house? Our heirloom is the eternal true mind or the Tathagatagarbha with its mysterious and clear awareness, not the material wealth with form and form of the world. Self-nature is full of Buddha-treasures, Dharma-treasures and Sangha-treasures, and is the "true treasure." In addition, diligently cultivating Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom, completing the Three Anasrava Studies, is also our "True Dharma Treasure".

Someone said: "This treasure, the precious asset that you talked about, cannot be seen, so how can I believe it?" This person is not to blame, because "this treasure" has no form, so it cannot be seen. However, we can still feel it, people with wisdom faculties will know immediately, and people without wisdom faculties cannot know. That's because their wisdom base is not yet mature and mature, so they cannot give rise to faith and cannot have clear understanding!

You Shouldn't Have a High and Arrogant Attitude Toward the Three Jewels!

According to Buddhism, lay people must respect monastics, not " consider the sky as equal, " must not despise monastics, and must not criticize monastics. Lay people must know how to make offerings to and praise monks, so that they do not create arrogant karma (arrogant karma); Otherwise, lay people will become arrogant and arrogant. Not only will they not gain merit, but they will also commit crimes. According to the law of Cause and Effect, they will definitely fall into the three evil paths. On the contrary, when receiving offerings from lay people, helping them plant merit fields, the monastic needs to reflect and consider every day whether he is practicing properly or not, because:

Donor one lak mi,

As important as Tu Di mountain,

The truth is that there is no practice of the Way,

Suffered from hypothyroidism!

(A grain of rice from a donor,

Heavy as Mount Meru,

Eating and not practicing,

Wear feathers, wear horns!)

When monastics receive respect from others, they must know how to self-reflect, do they themselves deserve to receive respect? My body wears the clothes of a monk, but am I no different from other people? Do I often generate useless delusions every day? Am I always angry and frustrated from morning to night? Is it true that from morning to night I am always jealous or obstructing the practice of others? If a monk commits the above things, he is not qualified to receive offerings from lay people. Even if he accepts them reluctantly, he will still feel ashamed. People who become monks and practice the Way need to always pay attention and not waste time in Bodhimanda. If we live like that and receive offerings from lay people, it is extremely wrong!

Why should lay people make offerings to ordained people or protect ordained people? That's because monastics are dedicated to cultivating the Way, without delusions, afflictions or jealousy like ordinary people. If we can do so, then we will be worthy of the respect and offerings of lay people, and we will be able to receive them without shame. If a monastic person does not truly practice, or is not even as respectful and sincere as a lay person, then he is not qualified to receive respect and offerings from others! This is something that everyone needs to be deeply enlightened about, they cannot " confuse fish eyes with pearls, " should not live in Buddhism to earn a living.

When lay people make offerings to monastics, they must not have a discriminatory mind, must not have a mind of choice: "This Master practices, so I want to make offerings. That teacher is not virtuous, so I don't make offerings." Don't have such an inappropriate state of mind. No matter where we are, we should make offerings to the Three Jewels, and not look for faults or faults in the Three Jewels. If you always look for the mistakes of the Three Jewels, then that is your arrogant ego at work. You are definitely not qualified to protect the Three Jewels!

In Bodhimanda, we should not commit sins but should do many meritorious deeds, so that we can make up for the sins we committed in the past. First, we need to repent, because:

Heavenly sin,

The most convenient repentance.

(Sin, no matter how great it is, fills the sky,

If you know how to repent, your sins will disappear.)

So how to repent? We must, in front of the four assemblies, tell all the sins we have committed, clearly state all the details of the sins, and vow that from now on we will absolutely not commit them again. Only then can the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas forgive us and help us eliminate our karma. Our previous sins were all "committed mindlessly, " meaning they were committed unintentionally. However, from now on, if we commit the same crime again, it is "intelligence of intentional violation" - knowing clearly but still intentionally violating - then even repentance will not be effective because it is a type of karma, in the future we will definitely suffer retribution. We should not have the mindset: "Commits crimes during the day, prays at night, and is considered innocent!"; Then just keep creating karma, and after doing it, continue to pray, and gradually form a mechanical habit. If we continue like that, our future karma will pile up like Mount Meru, how can we not fall into hell!

In our Bodhimanda there are incarnations of the ten directions

Buddha, the reincarnation of the Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, the reincarnation of the Bodhisattvas

Bich Chi Buddha, reincarnations of Arahants, and also

Thien Long Bat Bo is also here protecting the dharma. Therefore, if we in Bodhimanda always cause trouble for others, pointing out the mistakes of the ten directions! Living in Bodhimanda while cultivating on the one hand and creating karma on the other - the merits cultivated are not equal to the negative karma created, just like the money deposited in the bank is not equal to the money spent; If the deficit cannot be compensated, the future will be bankrupt. Bởi vậy:

Good and evil are two things,

Cultivate for the purpose of practice, create for the purpose of creating.

(There are two paths between good and evil,

If you practice, you practice, but when you create, you still create.)

That means good and evil are two paths. On the one hand, you practice, but you still create bad karma. Therefore, do not stay at the temple and only know how to create bad karma. You should regularly look for your own mistakes, not nitpicking the mistakes of others. If you keep looking for other people's faults and hindering others from practicing, not only will you not get anything good, but you will also have to suffer karma and unpredictable consequences in the future!

tieu_de: Avoid using polite words
tom_tat: In society there are many talkative people. Why? Because between people and people, in society, a climate has formed that does not dare to speak the truth, but only speaks lies
noi_dung:
Use less polite words

In society there are many talkative people. Why? Because between people and people, in society, a climate has formed that does not dare to speak the truth, but only speaks lies!

Why don't people speak the truth? Because no one wants to hear the truth! The same goes for France, many people only like flowers and leaves, not fruits! For example, fruit trees, when in flower, emit a gentle fragrance, everyone enjoys smelling it even more than eating it. But when the fruit is ripe, it no longer has such great attraction. This is similar to how people like to listen to lies and hate to listen to the truth. False words are like the fragrance when a tree blooms, they are all clever push and pull, polite and untrue words, but there are many people who want to listen, and listen passionately and with pleasure! And if we honestly talk about issues such as how to keep the Precepts, how to keep the rules, how not to fight, not to be greedy, not to seek, not to be selfish, not to take personal advantage, not to lie, or how to become a true Buddhist, not only people of other religions but also Buddhists will think that " is harsh, " feels uncomfortable in their hearts, and does not want to listen. Why so? It's because " is against the ear, " is straightforward, but this ear is not favorable for what they do! It is also for that reason that in the Linh Son Dharma Assembly, when Buddha Shakyamuni's disciple, Venerable Sariputta, invited him to preach the Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma, he taught:

Just, just, no practice!

The Dharma is wonderful and difficult.

(Stop, stop, don't say it!

My Dharma is wonderful and inconceivable.)

The Buddha said so, but Venerable Sariputta still attentively requested the Dharma. Buddha taught again:

Just, just not convincing!

The Dharma is wonderful and difficult.

(Stop, stop, don't say it!

My Dharma is wonderful and inconceivable.)

No matter how many times the disciple requested, the Buddha answered the same way. Finally, because the Dharma requester was so sincere, the Buddha was moved by compassion and compassion for Sentient Beings, so he preached the doctrine "Opening the Power to Manifest Reality,", setting out a temporary means to lead to the ultimate truth:

There is only one Buddha Vehicle, with no excess wings! (There is only one Buddha Vehicle, there is no other Vehicle!)

After the Buddha said that, five thousand people immediately withdrew from the Dharma Assembly! You see, some of those people were Buddhist disciples who had been cultivating the Way for many years, some had just learned the Buddha Dharma, all at the same time stood up and left the Dharma Assembly, not wanting to listen to the Buddha's wonderful teachings!

The above event proves that people only like to listen to lies and do not want to listen to the truth. Therefore, the words I say to you today are false and not true; You can forget all the above words. However, you need to remember carefully the dharma you want to hear, the dharma you want to practice!

All people who come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must follow the rules of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. Regardless of whether they are permanent residents of the Holy City or outsiders visiting the temple, no one is allowed to eat meat, smoke, drink alcohol, and even less smoke opium within the grounds of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. One more thing everyone needs to note is that they should not "thank" each other! The two words "thank you" are the next social words. That's the point of what I'm saying today, regardless of whether you want to hear it or don't want to hear it, I'm still saying it!

(June 26, 1983)

tieu_de: Appreciate the Grace of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas
tom_tat: The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas did not hesitate to turn the boat of compassion back to the Saha world to educate and tame Sentient Beings. They use eighty-four thousand dharma methods to guide those who are predestined. But, I don't…
noi_dung:
Cảm Kích Ân Ðức của Chư Phật và Chư Bồ Tát

The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas did not hesitate to turn the boat of compassion back to the Saha world to educate and tame Sentient Beings. They use eighty-four thousand dharma methods to guide those who are predestined. However, not only do we not understand the spirit and compassion, joy and forgiveness of Buddha and Bodhisattva, we also turn our backs on enlightenment, join the foolish world, abandon the roots and follow the branches, not wanting to end birth and death and escape the Three Realms!11

Everyone knows that the Three Realms are like a burning house, not a safe place, but no one wants to leave the Three Realms! Mặc dù biết rằng ở trong Tam Giới thì vạn phần thống khổ, nhưng ai cũng lưu luyến, chẳng muốn lìa xa. Họ sống một cách thản nhiên trong căn nhà lửa Tam Giới, chẳng lo âu sợ hải, lại còn cho là vui vẻ, sung sướng!

Chư Phật Bồ Tát hết lòng thuyết Pháp, dạy dỗ Sentient Beings, khiến quay về đường ngay nẻo phải. Unfortunately, Sentient Beings, because they do not understand the thoughts of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, listen but do not understand, look but do not see, consider your teachings as the wind passing through their ears, do not pay attention to memorization, still pretend " to live, drunk and dead, " is like a corpse that can walk or be eaten by meat that can run! Tuy là tu Ðạo, nhưng họ không biết tìm cầu con đường giác ngộ chân chánh. Vậy, nếu muốn tìm cầu con đường dẫn tới sự giác ngộ chân chánh thì tìm ở đâu? It's extremely simple, just don't turn your mind outward to pursue, but go against the delusion and return to enlightenment. Từ cảnh giới mê muội mà quay trở lại, đó chính là giác ngộ!

If one can abandon evil thoughts and return to mindfulness, Sentient Beings can become enlightened and open up great wisdom. However, Sentient Beings do not want "beginning" to return but just want to float in the sea of ​​samsara and suffering, forever losing the true path, and then think that such action is very legitimate. Isn't that crazy? Faced with that situation, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have no means to help Sentient Beings stay away from suffering and enjoy peace and joy. Why? Because Sentient Beings are still confused, too confused, not yet awakened! Teaching about the principles of enlightenment, everything is strange to them, the reason is because the bad habits accumulated in them are too deep. These habits override wisdom, obscure it, so they cannot perceive and clearly distinguish what is right, what is wrong, what is right, what is evil, what is real, what is fake.

If you know the truth, you should throw away the falsehood. Why are Sentient Beings confused? It's because we don't have true wisdom that wherever we go, we bump into walls, bump into walls, encounter obstacles, and things don't go smoothly. If we don't hit the east wall, we also hit the west, south, or north wall. If there's an open path in the middle, you don't go. You just keep banging your head against the wall until blood flows all over your face, but you still don't know " reflects the light, " doesn't know how to use wisdom to illuminate your mind!

Buddhas and Bodhisattvas wholeheartedly teach and preach many Dharma treasures 'Tripitaka and Twelve Sutras', yet Sentient Beings remain indifferent as if they did not hear or see, letting down their compassion, making them feel extremely tired. Why are they tired? Because they feel that Sentient Beings are difficult to save, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have expended so much effort, but Sentient Beings are still " as inert as wood and stone, " refuses to change, refuses to practice, refuses to keep the Precepts. Even though Sentient Beings are so difficult to save, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are still not discouraged. Even though it is difficult to save, they still save! Not only that, he also compassionately wants to save all Sentient Beings. How can we repay this kindness?

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva once made a vow that: Hell is empty, vow not to become Buddha, Sentient Beings are brought to an end, and Bodhi is attained. (Hell is not yet empty, I swear I will not become a Buddha, only after being saved by Sentient Beings will I attain Bodhi.)

How great is this prayer! Let's ponder the meaning of that prayer. There is no need to read the sutras, just listen to the prayers, we should already be grateful for Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's kindness, we should cry loudly in pain, thanking the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas for their care and protection for us. Everything in this world is created by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who sacrificed their lives in countless eons. We must definitely develop a great Bodhi mind in the pursuit of Buddhahood, under the level of Sentient Beings. Only then can we repay some of the grace of the Buddhas, the grace of the Bodhisattvas, the grace of our parents, the grace of our teachers, and the grace of heaven and earth. We must be a messenger for the Buddha, must develop a compassionate mind on behalf of the Buddha, so that Hsuan Hua promotes the Dharma, educates Sentient Beings and saves the country and people in a meaningful way. At all times, we must maintain compassion, have a spirit of righteousness, and be ready to use all our strength, no matter how small, to propagate the Buddha Dharma, to achieve the original mission of the Buddhas.

Why, after becoming a Buddha, did the Buddha not forget Sentient Beings and vowed to save Sentient Beings? That's because all Sentient Beings have Buddha nature and can become Buddhas, it's just that Sentient Beings don't know it yet! Due to being obscured by greed, anger, ignorance, ignorance, afflictions, delusions, etc., our true wisdom cannot be revealed; For that reason, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas come to show us the method of enlightenment. If we can practice according to His teachings and practice, then we will definitely gain wisdom. Therefore, at any time we must know how to appreciate the gratitude of the Buddhas, the gratitude of the Bodhisattvas, the gratitude of our parents, and the gratitude of our teachers.

In our universe, the Three Tai Tai: heaven, earth and humans all have equal value; So don't waste the value of life! That is the thought that a human being needs to have. We need to understand the original desires as well as the vows of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, because only then will our human life not be in vain!

(July 9, 1983)

How To Get More Intellectual Than Humans?

We must " borrow the false to cultivate the true, " must learn the superior wisdom and inconceivable supernatural powers of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

Why is it possible to reach a place of greater wisdom than others? How can one achieve inconceivable magical powers? In short, because when they still have the human earth, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas always practice seriously and honestly, and always keep the Precepts very carefully. At all times, they set an example for themselves, walking, standing, lying, and sitting in full dignity. As for Sentient Beings, they are not afraid of hard work, are willing to sacrifice, do not regret their lives, and absolutely never advertise themselves or brag about their merits.

He did it for the benefit of Sentient Beings. That is because They consider saving Sentient Beings to be Their duty and responsibility.

Buddhas and Bodhisattvas all have the thought:

Show mercy without asking for retribution,

Evil people do not repent.

(Thank you, don't expect anything in return,

Give it, no regrets.)

At the same time, they all have the act of "unconditioned great kindness, great compassion, " has immense compassion for those who have no affinity with them, seeing all living beings as the same body as themselves. It is thanks to such practice that they are wiser than others and achieve inconceivable supernatural powers.

If we often listen to Sutra lectures, we need to meditate and "digest" the meanings to be useful; Otherwise, even though you listen to the Sutras a lot, you will not be able to grasp the principles in the Sutras! There are many people who even put the meanings of the Sutra " behind their heads, " without studying or contemplating; Then, because they only used their own devil ",", the worm "clever", they caused all kinds of confusion and chaos. Doing such nonsense means that they are not filial to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and are not filial to their ancestors, parents and teachers. So what should we be like? You must practice the Buddha Dharma properly and honestly, not be lazy or sluggish, not be careless, be careful everywhere, always be cautious, and always be courageous and diligent, strictly following the Precepts. Those are the indispensable conditions that those who practice the Tao must follow.

If we have improper habits and habits, we must definitely change them. Having shortcomings that do not change and cover up, that is "supporting Tru and being abusive, " means helping King Tru do cruel and tyrannical things. During the An Dynasty, King Tru was originally an immoral king; Therefore, anyone who helps him do evil things means that person is "supporting the Emperor to do evil." Among those cultivating the Way, there is also the Emperor of Tru. Who is that? It's the Demon King! Seeing that the Buddha Dharma was flourishing, the Demon King was very upset, so he used thousands of methods to destroy the Buddha Dharma and disturb Bodhimanda. Whenever you have Bodhimanda, the Demon King will come and harass Bodhimanda. If you don't have Bodhimanda, the Demon King will disturb your body and mind, making you insecure and mentally unstable; Once your body and mind are crazy, you cannot practice systematically according to the Dharma.
