That is a direct way of sabotage. As for Ma's indirect sabotage

King is taking advantage of all kinds of realms to seduce, bewitch, and make you lose your concentration and your soul to go crazy. Because of the Demon King's poisonous scheme, you lost your true heart in cultivating the Way and by the time you regret it, it will be too late!

Therefore, people cultivating the Tao need to be as stable and steady as Mount Meru; No matter what realm you encounter, your heart will not be moved. At that time, the Demon King had no choice but to throw his armor and run away!

tieu_de: Learning the Precious Dharma in Practice
tom_tat: Every day when we study Buddhism together, everyone has something they enjoy, but if we don't practice it, it's useless. After studying, we must practice accordingly. Must practice with "feet firmly planted on the ground...
noi_dung:
Learning the Precious Dharma in Practice

Every day when we study Buddhism together, everyone has something they enjoy, but if we don't practice it, it's useless. After studying, we must practice accordingly. Must practice with " feet on solid ground, " to be able to enjoy. If we don't practice and just talk, then we're just like "the stone man" when it comes to Buddhism, it doesn't help much at all!

If we want to help the Buddha Dharma, we must propagate the Buddha Dharma, set an example for ourselves, pay attention to the four noble postures12 keep the five Precepts13 use the Four Immeasurable Minds (love, compassion, joy, equanimity) to save Sentient Beings and use the Six Great Principles (not fighting, not being greedy, not seeking, not being selfish, not self-seeking, and not lying) as standards to admonish ourselves. If you use such rules to propagate Buddha Dharma, then at any time and any place there will be the presence of the Dharma. There cannot be the appearance of the Ending Dharma. The evil spirits of pagans will be so scared that their hair will stand on end. Whenever they see your shadow, they will run away. What makes them afraid is not your magical powers but your virtue!

When "practice is unified, "knowing and doing are one, then your practice will definitely be successful; Demons and demons just listen to the sound and immediately surrender. Why is that? Because you have true wisdom, perceive truth and falsehood, know what to do and what not to do! You need to perceive clearly, understand thoroughly, not do crazy things, be free of all afflictions and troubles, then it can be said that you have reached the realm of "like being motionless, ever-clear." If you can do that, the Buddhas of the ten directions will applaud and be extremely happy; If that were not the case - not being able to reach the destination, resigning oneself to falling, not making progress - then the Buddhas would also burst into tears: "Oh! I have wasted so much spirit that even a Sentient Beings cannot save me. It's so difficult!" Therefore, if you know a little, practice a little, because " accumulating small things becomes a lot, contributing wind becomes a storm, " from a little accumulated, it will become a lot, for example, a pile of sand sometimes accumulates into a mountain, with enough effort, you will naturally succeed!

Being able to practice here means that God has "been very kind to me"; Therefore, I should not waste this precious opportunity and should not disappoint my master. Be brave and diligent in cultivating the Supreme Way to quickly attain Buddhahood!

Correct Your Mistakes, Your Karma Will Be Dissolved!

People living in the same place together means they have a relationship with each other, so don't get frustrated, angry, and even more so don't scold each other, such behavior is completely inappropriate and unacceptable. I hope everyone has the diligence and style of a gentleman.

Among the Six Levels, the 14 methods of Patience are the most important. Everyone must practice the Dharma of Forbearance and Humiliation to perfection in order to achieve success. A cultivator absolutely must not " light a fire in the liver, " must not get angry, must be patient in everything, because there is a saying:

Ignorance burns all merit and virtue.

(The fire of ignorance (anger) burns away the forest of merit)

Therefore, you must remember this point at all costs!

Today there was a disciple who asked to repent. I saw that the mistake was not very serious, so I told him that there was no need to go before the crowd to repent, just repent and correct his mistakes. The ancients said:

Concubine Thanh Hien, so talented?

Too much dan reform, good moc great peace!

Means:

Who is a Saint, who does not make mistakes?

Don't be afraid of modifications, what's better!

Knowing your mistakes and not making them again in the future is good, so say:

Being too capable of converting to nothingness.

(If there is a mistake, if you correct it, it will be erased.)

Knowing how to correct mistakes will no longer exist. That is, no matter how great the sin is, if you know how to repent, the sin will disappear (a great sin, if you repent, it will be easily eliminated). I'm just afraid that I know I'm wrong but still stubbornly believe I'm right; If something is wrong and accepted as right, it becomes even more wrong!

What I say today is not for any individual but for everyone. Regardless of whether anyone finds themselves in the above mentioned situation, they should quickly change it; If you don't fall into the above cases, then encourage yourself and take this as a motivation. Whenever we have an attitude that is not perfect and good towards others, we should immediately improve it.

You have come here (to the temple) thanks to many lifetimes ago cultivating good relationships and forming good relationships with each other; Otherwise, this life could not have gathered like this. That is something everyone needs to understand; Especially if you are a Buddhist, you should pay even more attention to the word "charm"! There is a proverb that says:

We have fate, we will meet again after a thousand miles,

No relationship, opposite each other don't know each other.

These two sentences are truly philosophical.

Fellow residents of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas should respect and help each other, not have an indifferent attitude. "crossed their arms and watched" or "stand on the other side and watch the house burn." Everyone should learn the spirit of the Bodhisattvas. When they see Sentient Beings immersed and miserable in the scene of "burning water and fire", they feel as if they themselves are suffering. Therefore, they seek to save Sentient Beings from the ocean of suffering, which is the duty of Buddhists. We should not be in the mood of "of happiness and misfortune," (rejoicing at the misfortunes of others). That is what I expect from all of you. I hope that everyone has a Bodhisattva heart, willing to forget themselves for others.

In every thought, we should always think of ways to support Buddhism, propagate Buddha Dharma, all for the sake of Buddhism. Be a true Buddhist, don't be afraid of hardships, don't be afraid of hardships, wholeheartedly support Bodhimanda. Only in Buddhism can one be a true Buddhist and be a true Buddhist. You need to have the ability to fight bravely in order to be able to " invincible battles; " cannot surrender as soon as you enter battle, unable to overcome the challenge. If you can pass the test, you are no longer far from the Way!

Concentration, Ma Fu

The nature of concentration, magic, and the tide of happiness,

False thoughts do not arise in the land of peace.

The mind only contemplates true wealth,

Lust destroys the field of merit.

Means:

Concentration, magic: happy day after day,

Not giving birth to false thoughts: a peaceful place.

The mind stops, thoughts stop - real wealth,

Eliminate desire - truly a blessed field.

Why do I have demonic obstacles? Because my nature is not yet determined! If our nature is determined, then we will always be lucid and clear, understanding everything. Once such level is reached:

Internally contemplate the mind, the mind is beyond the mind, Externally contemplate the form, form without the form.

That means at that time, when we look inside (internal insight) we don't see a mind, but when we look outside (external insight) we also don't see a body. At that time, both body and mind are "emptiness," and if you look far outside (far-sighted view), things also do not exist. All three types of body, mind and matter perish, at this time there is only reason "No".

The Middle Way arises based on this "No" principle. The Middle Way has no joy (joy), no anger (anger), no worry or sadness (anyone), no fear (concern), no love (love), no hatred (foul), no greed (lust). When the seven emotions (happiness, anger, regret, attachment, love, hate, desire) are no longer " aroused, " then there are no false thoughts inside, and there is no external greed, either inside or outside the body and mind are completely pure. That is the realm of "settled nature." Calm nature is the essence of the Middle Way.

When your nature is determined, you are as stable as a diamond mountain, no longer shaken by the realm of the seven emotions. If you see a happy scene and know it's happy, if you see an angry scene and know it's angry, it proves that you have not achieved concentration. When the realm comes, you immediately have attachments, likes or dislikes, that is due to your undetermined nature. These seven emotions are like ocean waves. If there are high waves, boats can capsize; If the wind is calm and the waves are calm, the boat will safely reach the dock. People cultivating the Tao must first understand the seven emotions thoroughly. It is not enough to just understand the principles and meanings of the seven emotions. It is necessary to control their temptations and suppress their evil effects. If you are not disturbed by the realm of the seven emotions, then your nature is already determined.

When the nature is determined, the demons will surrender and submit, they can no longer cause trouble, they cannot disturb the body and mind of people cultivating the Way. After subduing demons, when favorable circumstances come, I am happy, but when adversity comes, I am happy. Regardless of whether I encounter favorable or unfavorable circumstances, I am at peace and free. This peace is true peace, true happiness, not the peace that comes from external things. This taste of endless peace comes from within, so I am always happy, every day I am at peace, all worries, sadness or afflictions are no longer there.

Once our nature is determined, we always feel peaceful and no longer have false thoughts. When false thoughts no longer exist, everywhere will be peaceful, so say:

Dynamically reciting all existence,

Reciting the ten thousand things is nothing.

(Concept: all things exist,

Stop thinking: everything is empty.)

When we do not start thinking, our body and mind will naturally be pure and peaceful: therefore it is said:

The mind stops, thoughts stop - real wealth,

Desires eliminated - truly a blessed field.

That is the standard of cultivating the Way.

We should not " accept the enemy as our child" because the enemy can rob us of all our treasures, and we should also not listen to the devil, because they can trick us, and if we fall for the devil's trick, we will suffer great loss. Therefore, you should never make friends with the devil's relatives because they only know how to harm you and make you do crazy and deluded things.

The nature of a cultivator must be concentrated in order to leave delusion, return to enlightenment, and abandon evil to follow righteousness. If mindfulness is present at all times, there will no longer be any afflictions. When things happen, you should deal with them without worrying about fate; Thus, when the incident is over, the mind will be clean and clear, leaving no traces behind. You need to clearly understand the principle "three ungraspable minds" the past mind cannot be grasped, the present mind cannot be grasped, and the future mind cannot be grasped. After understanding it thoroughly, you need to follow it and practice to truly understand Buddha Dharma. If you study without practicing, no matter how much you study, it will be of no use. Ignorance and afflictions will still abound, and even in future lives there will be no corresponding place. True wisdom also does not represent money. Even if you have a little wisdom, it is just a shallow, superficial thing, not a true thing.

Everyone who cultivates the Way in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must know how to value time and not waste precious time, because:

The light of the day, the light of destiny.

(An inch of time is an inch of life.)

Therefore, we need to truly practice the Buddhist teachings we learned at Bodhimanda. Don't just do things to get things done or live in vain for days and months, because that goes against the Tao!

Only after we have concentrated our nature can we break through ignorance and reveal the Dharma nature. We must destroy ignorance and make the Dharma nature appear clearly in order to achieve the goal of learning Buddhism. The biggest taboo in studying Buddhism is that " has no beginning and no end, " has a beginning but no end, gives up halfway, and throws away all the hard work from before. We should not retreat in the middle of the road or stop and refuse to move forward; Otherwise, you will never reach "treasure" Buddha Dharma. Please remember: No matter what you do, there must be love and support; Don't let external circumstances cause you to waver and turn back, losing your aspirations! Making a vow and establishing a will must be like iron and stone; Don't be swayed by adversity and unsatisfactory things and forget the Bodhi mind. Losing the Bodhi mind is the greatest loss; Therefore, a true person who clearly understands the Buddha Dharma will resolutely preserve the Bodhi mind in any situation and will never regress the Bodhi mind.

If you don't understand the method of practice, then whatever you do, " will be the head of a tiger and the tail of a snake. " is incomplete, at first it is very enthusiastic and brave, but later it becomes lazy and complacent. That's called

" has no beginning and no end." Nothing is complete or perfect. Why is that? Because like cause and effect, Cause and Effect are not wrong one bit. Having studied Buddhism, we must believe in Cause and Effect, must not make mistakes about Cause and Effect, and even more must not refute, saying that there is no Cause and Effect. You must know that Cause and Effect is an eternal law that does not change!

(July 10, 1983)

tieu_de: Filial piety and sincerity touches Heaven and Earth
tom_tat: In Dai Nam Cau village, a village south of Hop Tan city, Northeast, there was a filial son named Cao, named Duc Phuoc. Because his mother was seriously ill, both Chinese and Western medicine were unable to cure him, so he discovered...
noi_dung:
Filial and Sincere Heart Touches Heaven and Earth

In Dai Nam Cau village, a village south of Hop Tan city, Northeast, there was a filial son named Cao, named Duc Phuoc. Because his mother was seriously ill, both Chinese and Western medicine were unable to cure her, so he vowed to cut off her hand and worship Buddha, asking for her mother's illness to be relieved. That filial piety moved heaven and earth, causing his mother to be resurrected from death. This event once caused a stir; Everyone knows Cao Duc Phuoc's filial example. It happened like this:

Cao Duc Phuoc's mother was seriously ill, did not eat rice, did not drink water, was barely breathing, and was dying. Anxious for his mother, Cao Duc Phuoc went to Tam Duyen pagoda (that day was Buddha's birthday, the pagoda was holding a Dharma conference, with about a few hundred good men and women attending). After lighting incense and bowing three times to Buddha, he pulled out a cleaver. Right when he was about to cut off his left arm, someone noticed it in time and immediately stopped him, asking: "Why do you want to cut off your hand?" Cao Duc Phuoc explained that it was because of his mother's illness and he wanted to cut off his hand to make offerings to Buddha. At that time, Lay Buddhist Ly Canh Hoa told him: "You should quickly go to the monk's office to pray to the Venerable. He has supernatural powers, maybe He can save your mother from her illness!"

Cao Duc Phuoc then went to the staff's office, asked to meet the Venerable and told the story in detail. The Venerable told him: "Go and request Master An Tu. He has a way to cure your mother's illness!"

Cao Duc Phuoc immediately came to my room and asked me to be compassionate and treat his mother. Because I heard that he was a filial son, I accepted and told him: "Just ride your bike home first. The teacher will come soon!" He ​​happily left immediately. Because he was riding a bicycle, he had to follow the main road; I took the shortcut on foot, so I arrived ten minutes before him.

As soon as he entered the house and saw that I was there, Cao Duc Phuoc was extremely surprised and asked: "Master! How did you come before me? You walk faster than I ride a bicycle!" At that time, the whole family, from old to young, came to pay homage to me; really:

Always burn incense,

Temporarily cover Buddha's feet!

(Usually refuses to burn incense,

Hug Buddha's feet when in danger!)

At that time, I wrote a prayer asking for Cao's mother to be healed. After burning the note, the patient slept peacefully and everyone went to rest. The next morning, the patient sat up and called his child by his family name: "Cu, Cu, my child, I'm very hungry, I want to eat some porridge!" Cao Duc Phuoc heard his mother's voice calling him, he was extremely happy, and hurried to cook porridge immediately. The patient finished a bowl of porridge and was fully awake and able to talk (for the past eight days the patient had been lying in a deep sleep, not saying a word, not eating or drinking, his lips were dark and his tongue was also black).

Cao Duc Phuoc asked: "Dear mother, how have you been feeling these past few days?"

His mother replied: "Oh! Mom was lost and couldn't find her way home. Everywhere she saw was a thick black screen, no sun, no moon, no stars. I don't know where east, west, south or north are anymore. Mom kept groping in that darkness for countless days, until last night when suddenly a monk came to take her home!"

When Cao Duc Phuoc heard his mother say that, he guessed and understood what was going on, so he asked again: "Mom! What did that monk look like?" His mother answered: "That monk wore a robe that was torn and patched in many places!" Cao Duc Phuoc pointed at me and asked: "Look, mom, is it this monk?" She looked at me intently, then said: "That's right! This monk is the one who brought mother home!"

Afterwards, Cao Duc Phuoc's entire family came to ask for refuge with me; His mother also gradually recovered.

(July 15, 1983)

tieu_de: Bo Shun Burning Bodies Offering to Buddha
tom_tat: When I was in the Northeast (Manchuria), I accepted a disciple, whose Dharma name was Guo Shun. His original family name is Dieu; People often call him "Old Dieu." He lives in Dai Nam Cau village, twenty miles south of Hebin city.…
noi_dung:
Body Burning Bodhisattva to Worship Buddha

When I was in the Northeast (Manchuria), I accepted a disciple, whose Dharma name was Guo Shun. His original family name is Dieu; People often called him "Old Dieu." He ​​lived in the village of Dai Nam Cau, twenty miles south of Hebin city. Before taking refuge in the Three Jewels, Lao Dieu was a wanderer, without a job. He not only smoked opium but also injected opium, it could be said that alcohol, gambling, sex, there was nothing he missed!

At that time, Japan was dominating the Northeast region, establishing Manchuria, and establishing the Qing dynasty's deposed emperor, King Tuyen Thong, as Emperor of Manchuria. However, in reality, Emperor Tuyen Thong was just a puppet king, because the entire government system was manipulated by the Japanese. In order to prevent the Soviet Union's invasion (of China), Japan built a defense project on the banks of the Hac Ha River and searched everywhere to capture people to work. Workers must contribute their efforts but receive absolutely no remuneration. Anyone sent to a labor camp is sad and depressed all day long, because they don't know when they will be able to return to their hometown. Hearing about life in the labor camp, everyone shivered, so scared that they were not cold but shivering! That place is truly a hell on earth with unspeakable suffering!

At that time, Qua Thuan was an unemployed wanderer, so he was captured by Japanese soldiers and taken to a labor camp on the side of the Bac Ha River. During the day, we have to work as hard as a buffalo or a horse; At night, he only sleeps with a sack made of sedge fibers, unable to withstand the cold. Therefore, he was always thinking and looking for ways to escape from the barracks. All four sides of the labor camp are surrounded by fences with strong electricity, any living thing that touches them will be electrocuted and die instantly. Despite the threat of the electric fence, because he could not stand the cruel and inhumane treatment of the Japanese soldiers, he was always on the lookout for opportunities to escape.

One night, because Guo Shun wanted to find freedom, despite all the dangers, he decided to leave the labor camp. Right when he was about to escape, suddenly an old man with white hair and beard appeared and told him: "Now is not the time; Wait until your suffering is over then I will let you know. I hope you will pay special attention, don't miss the opportunity!" Having finished speaking, the old man disappeared. Guo Shun followed the old man's words and returned to the barracks to wait.

About two weeks later, Qua Thuan dreamed of an old man with white hair and beard telling him: "Today is your chance to escape. There is a white dog outside the door, please follow it. Absolutely no loopholes. Please remember carefully! Remember!" Guo Shun woke up, both happy and scared. When I got outside the door, I saw that there was indeed a white dog waiting; He then followed the old man's instructions, letting the dog go first, and he followed closely behind. When he reached the electric fence, the dog quickly jumped over. That action seemed to give Guo Shun a hint, and he immediately imitated the dog. At that time, Qua Thuan was "spiritually blessed" (when luck comes, the mind is naturally clear and sharp), he cleverly took the rush bag he was using to protect himself from the cold, put it on the electric fence, then crawled over the fence. Having safely escaped from the tiger's den, he looked back and could no longer see the white dog. Perhaps the gods had helped him.

To avoid being pursued by Japanese soldiers, Qua Thuan had to hide in the jungle during the day. When thirsty, he drank stream water, when hungry he ate grass and leaves, and waited until night before daring to continue. After many arduous days like that, he was able to return to his old village. After enduring all that fear and hardship, he felt that human life was suffering, so he decided to become a monk and practice the Way. He went to temples but no one accepted him. When he arrived at Tam Duyen Pagoda, because they saw him dressed in rags, people thought he was a beggar and came to ask for ordination for the sake of life; Therefore, I also do not want to accept him.

Just when Guo Shun was in a situation where "big pagodas did not accept, small pagodas did not accept", suddenly a "monster,", looked like a beggar. The monster claims to be an expert practitioner who knows magic "36 Heavenly Cang,

Earth assassin, " can ride clouds and rain, can call rain and call wind, can cure all incurable complications, has " magic techniques to restore spring, " brings the dead back to life... He advertised himself, boasted for a while but no one believed him. However, Guo Shun trusted him and respected him as his teacher; then used the money he earned through illegal means to serve him. After a while, discovering that he had no skills at all and was just a scoundrel, Guo Shun left.

One day, I went to Dai Nam Cau village to treat Lay Buddhist Cao Duc Phuoc's mother. Her illness was very serious, both Chinese and Western medicine were helpless and unable to treat her. I then used the blessing mantra, and the result was that I was cured without medicine. The whole village knew this news and considered it a miracle. Old Dieu (aka Guo Shun) found out about this and immediately came to me and knelt before me, refusing to stand up, begging me to accept him as a monk disciple. At that time, I didn't pay any attention to him and just sat with my face pressed against the wall. About an hour later, I looked back and saw him still kneeling there. I asked him: "What are you doing?"

replied: "Master, please have mercy on me and accept me as your disciple."

I said: "You want to follow me to become a monk? But I have no virtue, nor any skill to teach you; I'm afraid it will only disappoint you!"

said: "Teacher, as long as you accept me as your disciple, I will be satisfied. I don't wish for anything else."

I said: "Becoming a monk is a very painful thing, you have to endure things that others cannot endure, you have to endure things that others cannot endure, you have to endure hardships that others cannot endure, you have to endure abuse that others cannot endure, can you bear it? If you can bear it, I will accept you as a disciple; If you can't do it, don't follow me to become a monk!"

Old Dieu immediately replied without hesitation: "Teacher! I can endure all hardships and hardships. Although becoming a monk is difficult, I firmly believe that it is not as miserable as living in a labor camp. I believe I can endure it!"

Through that conversation, I realized that he could indeed endure suffering; Therefore, I took him to Tam Duyen Pagoda, ordained him as a novice monk, and told him to work in the kitchen. Guo Shun worked very carefully, and was also very diligent in his studies. However, because he did not have good relationships with fellow monks and nuns, he was often bullied by them. Guo Shun then said to me: "Master! The brothers and sisters scolded me for no reason; So what should I do?"

I answered: "If you can't bear it anymore, you can practice alone."

Next to the Dragon King temple at the foot of Tay Son mountain, Dai Nam Cau village, there was an empty plot of land, so Qua Thuan built a thatched house there as a place to practice. The day the cottage was finished, Guo Shun came to Tam Duyen Pagoda and invited me to consecrate the Buddha statue. I brought a few disciples along. At night, ten dragons (turned into humans) came to ask for refuge. It was at the beginning of summer, the weather was dry and there was no rain, so the fields were dry and the grass burned and the rice seedlings turned yellow. Farmers - people who only depend on heaven for food - are all fed up and complaining; Sometimes I silently ask the sky, begging the heavens to be merciful and merciful to give me a few drops of water "nectar."

I asked the Dragons: "Your job is to make rain, but why is it so dry? Why doesn't it rain?"

The Dragons replied: "Master! Without orders from the Jade Emperor, we would not dare to make it rain. If we disobey orders, we will be punished."

I said: "Go to the Jade Emperor's Linh Tieu Bao Palace and ask the Great Emperor to be merciful and let rain fall within forty miles around this place. If it rains tomorrow, you can take refuge the day after tomorrow. Those are our terms of exchange!"

The next day, there was indeed rain pouring down within a forty-mile radius. The rice seedlings were soaked with rainwater and became lush, and the food harvested in the fall was even more abundant than in previous years. The next day, the Dragons came to the cottage and went to the front of the main hall to receive the Three Refuges. To commemorate this incident, I specially named that cottage "Long Vu Mao Bong" (Raining Dragon Thatched House), and wrote the name on a sign to hang in front of the door.

After that, Guo Shun vowed to burn his body to make offerings to the Buddhas. He prepared firewood and gasoline, then sat on the firewood and poured gasoline into the fire, his body burned to ashes. The next day, the villagers discovered that Long Vu Mao Bong had been burned, so they went to check and saw that although Qua Thuan's body had turned to ash, his heart was still intact, not burned by the fire. Everyone was praising endlessly; and then buried Guo Shun's ashes and heart on the spot.

Everything in the world must go through the stages of Creation, Persistence, Destruction, Emptiness - birth, existence, decay, and finally destruction - just like that, in a cycle without interruption. If you fully understand this principle, you will not have attachments or afflictions because of anything in this world. If you could "see through" and then let it all go, there would be no problem at all!

tieu_de: Cause and Effect Cause Qua Power to Leave Home
tom_tat: One year in the winter, because of Buddhist matters, I had to go to the south of Hebin city. Passing by an inn, because the innkeeper was my refuge disciple, I stopped by to visit. He said to me: "Master! In the shop...
noi_dung:
The Cause and Effect of Enlightenment

One year in the winter, because of Buddhist matters, I had to go to the south of Hebin city. Passing by an inn, because the innkeeper was my refuge disciple, I stopped by to visit. He said to me: "Master! In my inn, there is a guest who is a vegetarian. He wants to become a monk but has not found any temple. Maybe Master could accept him as a disciple?"

I asked: "Why does he want to become a monk?"

He replied: "Master! He is from Shandong, works as a tailor, and lives with a girl addicted to opium. One day, while he was away, the girl took all of his savings and ran away. At night, when he returned home, he realized that both his body and his belongings were gone! Because of such a heavy blow, he became depressed, felt that human life was meaningless, and only wanted to become a monk and practice. He went to the Pure Land Temple in Nam Cuong, Hop Nhi city, intending to ask for ordination with Master Nhu Quang, but Master Nhu Quang did not want to accept him as a disciple. He reluctantly had to stay at my inn, all day long his face was gloomy, unhappy, and he never talked to anyone; What a pity!"

Hearing that, I told the shop owner: "Tell him to come out!" The shop owner immediately went to call, but he refused to come out, perhaps because he saw that I was dressed in rags, and didn't look like a Venerable with a temple! The second time he called, he reluctantly came out; When he opened his mouth, he immediately asked: "What did you call me here for?" (Shandong people are usually honest and straightforward, so why do you think like that.)

I told him: "I came here to find you!"

He was extremely surprised and asked again: "Do you know me?"

I said: "Let's not talk about that. Do you want to become a monk? My temple currently needs someone to take care of food and water; You can take that as an opportunity to practice asceticism. There is food for you to eat and a room for you to live in; But I don't have money to spend. So, do you want to go there?"

Because he heard me say I was willing to accept him as a disciple, he happily replied: "I'm ready to go now!" He immediately followed me back to the temple and took care of the cooking in the temple. Then he received the novice vows, his Dharma name was Qua Nang.

One day, Guo Nang became impulsive and spontaneously made a protest15 in a small room without first asking permission from the people in the temple. At that time, I was completely unaware of the inside story, but someone hinted in front of me: "Collecting disciples makes it impossible to teach them; What a loss of face! Not yet finished being a disciple, I wanted to become a Patriarch!" I was surprised, so I went to the back house to see what I was seeing and met a brother. He told me: "Your disciple rebelled, didn't keep the temple's rules, without permission, he arbitrarily created a protest!"

I went to Qua Nang's room and sure enough, I saw him meditating on the couch. Seeing me, he immediately walked down to pay his respects. I asked: "Who told you to make this resistance?"

Hao replied: "No one told me!"

I said: "If no one told you, why did you take it upon yourself like that? You broke the rules!"

Guo Nang didn't say anything, just knelt down quietly. I said: "Go to the Buddha's temple to repent, kneel until the incense sticks burn out!"

After I left, Guo Nang did not go to the Buddha's temple to kneel and incense, but instead went to the protest to sit and mend his clothes. Half an hour later, I arrived at the main hall and did not see Qua Nang kneeling there. I went to Qua Neng's room again and asked: "Qua Neng! Why don't you kneel?"

Guo Nang replied: "Wait a minute!"

I said: "If you don't kneel incense, I will kneel for you!" So I went to the Buddha's temple to burn incense and kneel on the bricks. Seeing me kneeling, Guo Neng had no choice but to come behind me and plead: "Master! I know my mistake, Master, please forgive me. Master, please stand up, I'm kneeling here!"

I said: "I can't teach my disciples, but I can still teach myself!" Since that teaching, Guo Neng has always followed the rules and practiced diligently. Qua Nang has the courage "knows mistakes and accepts correction." I hope you all also have the virtue of admitting mistakes and being willing to change!

Heaven's wealth cannot be wasted!

Someone asked me: "In your opinion, how many good men and women will participate in the Dharma Assembly of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva Achieving Enlightenment this time?" I answered: "Maybe only three or four people!" Today I counted and saw that there were more than four hundred people attending the Dharma conference; That person then asked me again: "Do you mean one hundred people when you say one person?" I said: "I don't know!"

This year at the Avalokitesvara Dharma Conference, the crowd was more sincere than in past years. In previous years at Dharma conferences, when eating, everyone talked loudly, not following the rules of the Tang Trai. In addition, many people throw away rice and leftover food in the trash; Or after eating, they don't rejoice in the merits and leave. This year the situation in general has improved a lot, people don't talk loudly and don't waste food, and very few people rush back to San Francisco, which is good news!

In the future, when there are Dharma conferences, it is necessary to remind everyone not to talk during mealtimes and to appreciate food and not to waste or throw away food. The ancients wrote the following poem:

Sour Hoa Nhat and Noon,

Khan extracted peace on the earth,

The middle tricuspid lobe is far away

Lala phase new suffering!

Means:

Harrowing the land under the noon sun,

Sweat drenched in rice flowers,

Who knows when carrying a bowl of rice,

Every grain, every hardship!

Most people in the world do not know the principle of "every grain, every hardship,"so they let the heavens waste their energy and freely destroy food. You should know that the reason many people do not have food to eat in this world is because in the past they wasted food, so in this life they have to suffer the retribution of not having food to eat. I need to state this simple principle for everyone to clearly understand so that they will no longer waste Chapter resources unreasonably.

Kitchen managers need to be wise, food and drinks prepared for the masses need to be nutritious and hygienic. You have immeasurable merit in serving the masses. Every day you have to check the refrigerator, see which foods are easily perishable and use them first, and which foods are not perishable, then keep them fresh for later use; Do not let the Chapter food rot and then throw it in the trash because that is creating a crime and causing karma. Everyone needs to be careful about this point!

Taking care of the people's eating and drinking, knowing how to regulate it properly, is meritorious; If you don't regulate it well, you will be guilty. Earning merit is easy, because it is only due to the way you work. If you follow the rules, you will have merit, if you do not follow the rules, you will be guilty. In short, both merit and sin come from one's own hands. If you know how to value it and don't waste food, then you have merit; If you spoil or throw away food unreasonably, you will be guilty of a crime!

(Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas,

July 24, 1983)

tieu_de: It is necessary to check published books
tom_tat: Dharma Realm Buddhist Association and Dharma Realm Buddhist University have published many books on Buddhism; However, there are some books that have not yet reached the point of perfection. From now on, no matter who explains the book...
noi_dung:
Need to Check Published Books

Dharma Realm Buddhist Association and Dharma Realm Buddhist University have published many books on Buddhism; However, there are some books that have not yet reached the point of perfection. From now on, no matter who explains or prepares the books, all books must be carefully checked before publication. Only after receiving everyone's consent and making sure that the book has no more errors can it be printed.

From now on, everything in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must be conducted with a democratic style, impartiality, fairness, impartiality, and with the spirit of progress in the direction of truth, goodness, and beauty. The books we publish are error-free; Because if there are mistakes, it will have a negative impact on everyone, and they will also be criticized. Therefore, I hope everyone will make an effort, try to make it perfect, and reach perfection.

Buddhist sutras contain teachings spoken directly from the mouth of Buddha Shakyamuni, therefore, not a single word must be changed, nor a single word left out, otherwise, not only will there be no merit, but on the contrary, it will also be a sin. The ancients taught that:

Explanatory medical literature,

The three worlds of Buddha's injustice,

Ly Kinh one word,

That means the same ghost theory.

Means:

Explanation according to the text:

Oan ba đời Phật.

Rời Kinh một chữ:

Thành lời ma nói.

From this we can see that translating the scriptures is not an easy job. We hope that everyone will do their best to translate the sutras so that they are completely in accordance with the Buddha's intentions and have no defects. Thus, once widely spread, these scriptures will help readers enjoy the benefits of Buddha Dharma!

Cultivating the Way is Necessary "True Blessings, Seek Hue"

When we Buddhist followers have not yet become Buddhas, we _need to know "to cherish blessings and pray for wisdom." Whenever we know to cherish blessings, blessings will increase, and if we pray for blessings, wisdom will increase.

Look: People in life have countless different situations. There are people who have great blessings, do not need to do anything but get everything they want, everything is available, life is very prosperous; They are not sad or worried, they are extremely happy, it is because they have cultivated many blessings in the past, so now they can enjoy such great blessings! Some people have very good memories, they only see it once and never forget it. They are both intelligent and healthy, and also have great eloquence; When they preached the Dharma, the phenomenon of "the sky raining flowers and the ground emerging with golden lotus" occurred. Vì sao họ có khả năng ấy? That's because in the past they practiced wisdom a lot!

How to cultivate wisdom and where to practice? First of all, start from the Mahayana, read and recite the Mahayana sutras, study the Tripitaka thoroughly, to the point of perfection, the mouth can recite, the mind can think. Morning and afternoon, if you grind the Tripitaka 16 every day until you understand it thoroughly, then great wisdom will be revealed, and in your next life you will definitely be both intelligent and eloquent.

We already know what is "to treasure blessings, to pray for favors", we need to cherish things and not damage them. Doing work such as repairing bridges, building roads, building pagodas, erecting stupas, donating clothes, donating food, and helping the poor means cultivating merit and creating a merit field. Also preaching the Sutras and preaching the Dharma, printing sutras for dissemination, translating sutras, painting Buddha pictures... belong to the dharma of cultivating wisdom. Suppose you don't want blessings and don't want wisdom, then there's nothing left to say. However, if you want blessings and wisdom, then quickly cultivate blessings and seek wisdom. Don't waste your blessings and don't give up your wisdom arbitrarily! "Rewarding blessings and praying for wisdom" is a great and indispensable task that every Buddhist believer needs to practice!

tieu_de: Hot-temperedness is a cause and effect that hinders the practice of the Way
tom_tat: There is a saying: "Defilement is Bodhi." Someone asked: "Then, if afflictions do not arise, will there be no Bodhi?" Not! Because affliction itself is Bodhi! What is Bodhi? Bodhi means no birth...
noi_dung:
Imtemper is a Cause and Effect that Obstacles Cultivation of the Way

There is a saying: "Affliction is Bodhi." Someone asked: "Then, if affliction does not arise, will there be no Bodhi?" No! Because affliction itself is Bodhi! What is Bodhi? Bodhi means not giving birth to afflictions! If humans only give birth to afflictions, then afflictions will still be afflictions and Bodhi will still be Bodhi, so do not misunderstand the meaning of the above sentence.

You must know that once you yourself reach the realm of truly having no more afflictions, no more ignorance, no more delusions, no more lustful thoughts, then even if you have a little hot temper, you can still be forgiven. However, of course the best thing is to not have a hot temper and live together happily, in harmony, and in solidarity with everyone, making everyone feel close.

People who practice the Tao should use virtue to inspire others, not use force to oppress them. You should speak morality to anyone, so that everyone wholeheartedly admires and admires you as a talented, ethical, educated, and compassionate person. Otherwise, if you are entangled in the cycle of fame and profit, you will be eighteen thousand miles away from the Buddha's path. You need to pay special attention to this point.

What is the practice of becoming a monk and cultivating the Way? It is cultivating the Way of Forbearance. Anyone who gets angry is going against the Tao, and will never be in harmony with the Tao. Being angry is a very bad quality, and is also a cause and effect for an obstacle on the path of cultivating the Way. Hope everyone is careful and absolutely should not make this mistake!

If a person becomes a monk and practices the Way without mastering the basics of the problem, his practice is like "cooking sand and hoping it will turn into rice."no matter how long he cooks, the sand cannot turn into rice! If you don't have "fire" ignorance, desire thoughts will stop. Why is that? You have lustful thoughts because in your heart there is "fire and anger." Therefore you keep feeling like this is "not possible, " that is also "not possible," many problems "cannot" happen to you. Therefore, people cultivating the Way need to eliminate all afflictions so that all troubles and obstacles will no longer exist!

(July 25, 1983)

tieu_de: Realm of Arahant Attainment
tom_tat: "Arahant, all effluents are completely destroyed, one can overcome afflictions, attain self-benefit, end all existence, and attain freedom in the mind.
noi_dung:
The Realm of the Arhat Attainment

In the Preface, Chapter One of the Lotus Sutra, it is written:

"A Arhat, all defilements are completely destroyed, all afflictions are overcome, one attains self-benefit, all beings are united, the mind attains freedom."

("Arhats have exhausted all defilements, no longer have afflictions, have reached the point of benefiting themselves, are free from all 'existence and cessation,' the mind is free.")

That is the realm of an Arahant who has attained enlightenment. Now let's briefly understand the meaning of the above passage.

"All defilements are completely ended" (all defilements are gone). "The defilements" here include talking a lot, listening a lot, seeing a lot of shapes and forms, and giving rise to a lot of false thoughts. What is "uncontaminated," or "uncontaminated?"In short, anasrava means:

Non-gifts,

Non-auditory gifts,

Non-gifts, words,

Animal offerings.

Means:

Don't look at it if it's against the rites,

If it's against the rules, don't listen,

Don't say anything that goes against the rites,

If it goes against the rites, don't do it.

Here, "ceremony" means rules and regulations; But the rules and regulations are also the Precepts. If you do not look at things that are contrary to propriety, your eyes will be pure. If you do not hear things that are contrary to propriety, your ears will be pure. If you do not say words contrary to propriety, your tongue will be pure. If you do not do things contrary to propriety, your body will be pure. When six senses

If (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind) are all pure, there will be no more gonorrhea. Having gonorrhea is like a water vase with a hole that allows the water in the vase to flow out, making the vase permanently unable to be filled with water. For cultivating the Way, the defilements are afflictions, impatience, and anger. If you cultivate a little merit but are burned away by the "fire" of ignorance, then you will never attain enlightenment. Everyone needs to pay attention to this point and practice carefully!

On the outside, it is as if it is motionless. On the inside, there are no thoughts of desire. That is a state where there are no more defilements. If the outside is "immobile" but inside is still passive, then it means there is still contraband. In other words, if you still have thoughts about desire and act according to desire, you still have defilements; If there is no more, it is anasrava. Cultivating the Dao means " cultivating anasrava, " is cultivating the practice of reversing the origin, returning to the original pure self.

The Great Arhats have purified all the dross, leaving only the essence, so it is said that they are completely free of all defilements.

"Overcoming afflictions" (no longer afflicted). An Arhat has no more afflictions. How to get rid of afflictions? The method is very simple: don't fight, don't be greedy, don't seek, don't be selfish, don't seek personal gain, don't lie! Thanks to doing so, the Arhats are completely free of all defilements and have no more afflictions.

"To gain personal benefit" (to reach one's own advantage). Arhats have achieved the benefits of "Meditation on micronutrition, abundant Dharma joy" (taking joy in meditation as food, and being filled with peace in the Buddha Dharma). They also achieved Samadhi of Non-Controversy, completely cutting off the mind of preferring to win or lose. There is a verse that says:

Competition wins over the heart,

The Dao of Data is infinitely similar,

Conveniently giving birth to the Four Generals of the Mind,

Why did he attain Samadhi?

Means:

Competing is about winning or losing,

Going against the Tao,

Giving birth to four forms of mind

How to attain Samadhi?

"All beings end" (all 'existence,' 'end'). "Huu"17 is the twenty-five sentient scenes18 in the Three Realms. "Conclusion"19 is the accumulation of birth and death due to afflictions. Due to delusions, delusions, worldly delusions, and ignorance, our escape from the Three Realms is hindered. If we can get rid of all bad habits, eliminate all afflictions that have gathered together, and end all problems in the Three Existences,20 that means we have "all existence, " ended the Samsara!21

"The mind enjoys freedom" (the mind is free). Why is that so? Because the mind is peaceful and free! Why is the mind happy and free? It's because " has finished all the defilements, no longer has afflictions, has reached the point of benefiting himself, finished all existence and ending." The Great Arhats have reached the realm of:

All defilements are destroyed, Pham-virtue is established,

The reason for doing so is that there is no afterlife.

(The defilements are gone, Pham-hanh22 has been achieved,

Everything is done, no more reincarnation.)

Our mind is free, not free. "Excuse me" means that the body is here but the mind is not here, if you don't think about the Southern Dynasty, you will go to the North, if you don't remember the east and west, you will dream about the north and south, from beginning to end there is never a moment to stop thinking. Those wandering thoughts chased away "host" and let "guest" rush in from outside to take control, so the mind is not at ease. "Freedom" means the mind no longer has distracting thoughts, the self-nature radiates bright light illuminating heaven and earth, body, mind, and head are pure, serene, and free.

The above passage is extremely important so we need to remember it and not forget it. If you study that Sutra Text thoroughly and thoroughly, I guarantee that you will be able to escape birth and death and attain the same realm as the monks.

That's La Han. Without attaining Arhatship, the mind cannot be at peace. Only when one attains Arahantship, chases away visitors, and gets rid of afflictions, will the mind be so free!

Why is it necessary to recite Buddha's name?

Vì sao lúc bình thường chúng ta cần phải niệm Phật? Lúc bình thường chúng ta thường niệm Phật là để chuẩn bị cho lúc lâm chung.

Thế thì tại sao không đợi đến lúc lâm chung rồi hãy niệm Phật? Tập quán là thói quen được huân tập qua nhiều ngày, nhiều tháng. Therefore, if you normally do not have the habit of reciting Buddha's name, when you die, you will not remember that you need to recite Buddha's name. Therefore, in normal times we need to learn to recite the Buddha's name and practice the Pure Land Dharma, so that when we die, we will not panic or panic, but on the contrary, we will be safely reborn in the Pure Land!

Vì sao chúng ta cần phải vãng sanh về Thế Giới Ultimate Bliss? That's because when Amitabha Buddha practiced as a monk in the human world, he made forty-eight great vows, which said:

"After I become a Buddha, if in the ten directions there are any Sentient Beings who recite 'A-Di-Da Buddha,' my name, then I will definitely lead that person to my world, and in the future, he or she will become a Buddha. In my world, everyone is born from a lotus flower, so their bodies are completely pure and immaculate."

Because Amitabha Buddha made such a great vow, all Sentient Beings should practice the Buddha's Recitation Dharma, a method that is very suitable for everyone's ability and is also very easy to practice. The Bible also teaches:

Ðời Mạt Pháp, một ức người tu hành hiếm khi có được một người đắc Ðạo; duy có tu Pháp-môn Niệm Phật là ai cũng được độ thoát.

nói rằng trong số một ức người tu hành, hiếm hoi lắm mới có một người đắc Ðạo; Only the Dharma-door of Buddha Recitation can help people be reborn in the Pure Land and thus be saved. Ðặc biệt là trong thời Mạt Pháp hiện tại, niệm Phật chính là pháp môn hợp với căn cơ của mọi người nhất.

However, Europe and America today are not in the Dharma Ending era but can be said to be in the Dharma era. Why is it said that Europe and America are in the era of Dharma? Vì Phật Pháp vừa mới được truyền tới các nước ở phương Tây và hiện đang vào lúc hưng thịnh. Do đó, hiện tại ở Mỹ quốc có rất nhiều người rất thích tham Thiền, tịnh tọa; That is also a manifestation of the Dharma.

Thời Chánh Pháp, ai cũng có thể tu Pháp-môn Niệm Phật. In the Dharma Ending Age, everyone can practice the Buddha's Recitation Dharma. In any era, we can practice this Dharma. Nếu như có người đối với các pháp môn khác không thể dụng công được, thì nên tu Pháp Niệm Phật. Thiền-sư Vĩnh Minh Diên Thọ có nói rằng:

True Zen, Pure Land,

Because it's like tiger urination.

(There is Zen, there is Pure Land,

Like a tiger grows horns.)

People who practice Zen and recite Buddha's name are like tigers that grow horns and are extremely majestic. They can:

Presently as a sphinx,

Future work of Buddha.

(In this life, I will be a teacher for everyone,

To become a Buddha in the future, to become a Patriarch.)

Therefore, a person who truly meditates is a person who truly recites Buddha's name, and a person who truly recites Buddha's name is also a person who truly meditates. Speaking a little more deeply, the person who truly observes the Precepts is the person who truly practices Zen, and the person who truly practices Zen is also the person who truly practices the Precepts. Then, the person who truly preaches the Sutras and preaches the Dharma, that is, the person who truly preaches the Sutras for the sake of preaching the Sutras, is also the person who truly practices Zen!

In the Evidence of Dao Ca, Great Master Vinh Gia said:

The heron sect is clear, the heron theory is clear, Concentration, and wisdom are completely unobstructed. (Tông cũng thông, Thuyết cũng thông, Ðịnh, Huệ sáng tròn chẳng trệ không.)

Vậy, người vừa biết tham Thiền lại vừa biết giảng Kinh là người thông suốt cả tông lẫn thuyết. To talk a little more deeply, the person who truly recites Mantras, who truly practices Tantra, is also the one who truly practices Zen. For that reason, although it is said that Zen, Education, Law, Secret, and Purity are the five methods, if we consider the source, they are all one and not different. If we talk a little more deeply, even "one" no longer exists, so how can there be "five"? Người chân chánh học Phật Pháp cần phải hiểu điểm này cho rõ ràng.

Those who tend to divide sects think that the Buddha's Recitation Dharma is the highest, while Meditation is incorrect; There are also people who say that Meditation is the highest Dharma, while Buddha Recitation is wrong. Those who have such notions are people who do not understand Buddha Dharma clearly. Must know that:

Nhất thiết giai thị Phật Pháp, giai bất khả đắc.

(Tất cả đều là Phật Pháp, đều không thể chứng đắc.)

Since " has no dharma that can be attained, " has no need to be attached to things that should not be attached to, if there is no problem, find more problems, or cause problems.

If you truly understand the Dharma, then "there is no Dharma that can be attained." However, for those who do not understand the Dharma and say that nothing exists at all, they will be disappointed. Therefore, the Buddha taught the Right Dharma23 to lead to Real Dharma24 and preached the Right Wisdom to lead to Real Wisdom.

So, what is Real Wisdom? Thực Trí là một "quy vô sở đắc," trở về lại chỗ không chứng đắc. True form, without form, but also without " without form, " is true wisdom!

Con Người Có Cần Trọn Ðạo Hiếu Hay Chăng?

Today let's study this issue: Why do people need to be filial to their parents? Need to be filial to parents or not need to be filial to parents? The problem has two explanations. Standing on the stance of dharma beyond the world, it is not necessary to be filial to parents. I believe that anyone who hears me say this will be extremely surprised, because they have never heard this word before. Mình vẫn biết, là người nào cũng cần phải hiếu thảo với cha mẹ, chưa hề nghe ai nói rằng không cần trọn đạo hiếu cả. So you feel surprised. Nhưng nếu căn cứ vào chân lý thì mình có thể nói như vậy: Ðứng trên lập trường pháp thế gian đương nhiên chúng ta cần làm tròn chữ hiếu. Pháp thế gian là mộc bổn thủy nguyên25 do đó mình phải thận chung truy viễn, nghĩa là hết lòng hiếu thảo với cha mẹ. Hiếu với cha mẹ, cung kính Sư trưởng là đạo lý của trời đất.

Nhưng nếu căn cứ vào pháp xuất thế mà nói chúng ta cần nỗ lực tu hành, dụng công học tập, phát đại tâm Bồ-đề thì đó là trọn vẹn đại hiếu, không phải là tiểu hiếu. How to explain this sentence? Bởi vì khi mình tu hành được thành công thì có thể siêu độ được bảy đời cha mẹ, khiến họ sanh lên cõi trời. Rằng: "Nhất tử thành Phật, cửu tổ thăng thiên." Nghĩa là khi một người con thành Phật thì chín đời tổ tiên được sanh lên trời. That's called grave unfilial transgression.

There are four types of filial piety: one is grave unfilial transgression, two is small filial piety, three is far-reaching filial piety, and four is close filial piety. What is grave unfilial transgression? That is, repaying the gratitude of one's parents many generations ago, and repaying the gratitude of one's master. What is petty filial piety? That is, being filial to your parents in this life only; Worrying about and taking care of your parents makes them happy, takes care of them, comforts them, that means respecting them and making offerings to them.

What is called filial piety? Tức là kính trọng các bậc thánh hiền xưa kia, lấy mỗi lời nói mỗi công hạnh của họ làm gương sáng để mình bắt chước noi theo. What is filial piety? That is, in addition to being filial to your parents, you also need to be filial to other people's parents. Rằng: "lão ngô lão, dĩ cập nhân chi lão," tức là tôn trọng những huynh trưởng, tiền bối của mình rồi cũng tôn trọng những bậc tiền bối của kẻ khác. We need to have such filial thoughts and actions.

The true dharma of the world surpasses filial piety, that's why I say: You should not be attached to filial piety. If we are attached to being filial to our parents, we still have loving thoughts and feelings. That's just a delusion. Cả ngày chỉ tưởng nhớ tới cha mẹ thì làm sao tu đạo? Therefore, according to the truth, one should not practice filial piety. When I talk up to this point, some people don't understand, some do, so everyone should study this issue deeply.

Currently, people's hearts are deteriorating day by day, and the Chapter's conduct is getting worse day by day. "Human hearts are not old,"people's hearts are not the same as before. Why is that? Because people are supposed to be filial to their parents, but they are not filial. They believe that filial piety is an outdated idea, that parents have a duty to raise their children. Therefore, they are not filial to their parents. Are they not properly cared for in order to practice? Nor is it. Nếu ai chân chính tu hành thì không cần thiết phải phụng dưỡng cha mẹ mà cũng được xem là đại hiếu. In the future, I will surpass my parents. But if you are not filial to your parents, do not practice, and only specialize in creating all kinds of evil karma, then in the future you will definitely fall into the three evil paths. There is no doubt about this anymore. Take a look! Nowadays, many young men and women learn cowardly habits. If they don't kill people and burn houses, they also commit adultery and heresy. There is no evil thing that they don't do. They think that doing such wanton and improper things is freedom. Họ cho rằng không cần phải hiếu thảo với cha mẹ mà nên học những điều xấu xa. Such thinking is so wrong! Although I can't cover it all, most young people make similar mistakes.

Although a cultivator is not completely filial to his parents, he has the ability to save his parents from the ocean of suffering and ascend to heaven. Nhưng cũng có những người không hiếu thảo với cha mẹ, cũng không tu hành. Every day, you keep doing unethical things, or destroying your family, or disturbing the country and society, and disrupting security and order. Ðó tức là tự mình chặt gốc, càng chặt gốc thì càng không còn chỗ đứng, tương lai không biết sẽ ra sao. Những việc làm xấu xa như thế là những hành vi tội lỗi khó mà tha thứ được.

Trên đây tôi có nói là tu hành có thể buông bỏ sự chấp trước vào cha mẹ, chuyên tâm nhất trí mà tu hành thì đó là điều đúng. However, if you do not practice or fulfill filial piety, that is wrong. Ðiểm này các bạn hãy nhận cho rõ ràng bởi vì: "Vạn ác dâm vi thủ, bách thiện hiếu vi tiên," trong vạn điều ác thì dâm dục là đứng đầu, trong một trăm điều lành thì hiếu thảo là trước hết.

(Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas,

July 29, 1983)

noi_dung:
What is Good Knowledge

Simply put, good knowledge means a wise person, evil knowledge means a foolish person. Good knowledge has righteous knowledge, evil knowledge has wrong knowledge, wrong views, wrong understanding, and evil ways. If something is in accordance with Buddha Dharma, then it is right knowledge, right view, true understanding. If something is not in accordance with Buddha Dharma, it is wrong knowledge and wrong view. A good wise man is someone who practices by relying on Buddha Dharma, while an evil wise man is someone who relies on magic to practice. Good and evil are different, the distinction is here.

Good-minded people use the Four Dharmas to educate Sentient Beings. What is the Four Methods of Photography? That is, almsgiving, loving speech, beneficial actions, and cooperation. These four dharmas can easily harmonize with Sentient Beings, causing Sentient Beings to develop interest in the Dharma and believe deeply in the Dharma.

Almsgiving: If you want people to believe in Buddha Dharma, you need to give alms and teachings, making them develop sympathy for you.

Loving speech: Words do not go against humanity, do not go against Buddha Dharma, the words we speak are benevolent and moral.

Benefits: Words, actions and thoughts according to conditions of practice bring benefits to Sentient Beings.

Colleague: For Sentient Beings who deserve to be saved, do the same work as them to educate them.

Those are four Dharmas that help us create sympathy and trust towards Sentient Beings. If one's words are in agreement with one's actions, for the common good and not for personal reasons, one takes one's body as an example, and boldly acts when encountering a meaningful matter, then Sentient Beings will naturally believe in one's words and also believe that the Buddha Dharma is the boat to escape the sea of ​​birth and death.

You come here to listen to the sutras and sermons, each of you is a person of great knowledge. You should understand that Bodhi's original nature has always been pure. In the past, purity meant not having created anything, nor being contaminated by anything. This Bodhi nature does not need further fabrication, it is already present like this, it has always been complete. This Bodhi nature is also Buddha nature. Please pay special attention to this point! Everyone has Buddha nature exactly like Buddha's, there is no difference. However, I am deeply ignorant and obscured by ignorance and delusion, so my Buddha nature cannot manifest. If you use wisdom to handle everything, Buddha nature will appear. At that time, you are a good-knowledgeable person.

noi_dung:
Talk Less, Use More Effort

Anyone who participates in the Buddha's Seventh, or the Zen's Seventh, or the Avalokitesvara Seventh, or the Ksitigarbha's Seventh is good; Don't propagate to people outside the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas that the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is good like that or that. We do not expect outsiders to know the good things about the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. Why is that? If others know, people will flock to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas from all directions. At that time, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas will have no way to respond. The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas always works silently, everyone endures hardships, and sincerely practices. Therefore, for outsiders, we should not focus on advertising propaganda. If this is a good place to practice, you can come often. If you feel bad, you should not follow this path anymore, that is the consistent Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas has six great Principles to guide practice, that is, do not compete, do not be greedy, do not seek, do not be selfish, do not seek personal gain, and do not lie. If you truly understand these six Principles, you will not have reached the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas in vain. There are some people who are very greedy for fame, but the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas does not need those people. Why? Because the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas wants to get rid of the five desires: wealth, form, fame, food, and loins. These five desires are the root of hell, but most people in the world love those things, but the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas wants to escape those bonds. Therefore, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas does not want to be famous, nor does it seek any profit, only relying on genuine practice to propagate Buddha Dharma and continue the Buddha's wisdom. That is the general situation of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

tieu_de: When meditating, you need to remember that at all times
tom_tat: This Meditation Hall begins, I hope you bring all your spirit to meditate. Please develop a strong mind to meditate. Always remember to meditate, remember how to escape birth and death, and forget to eat and drink to meditate...
noi_dung:
Meditation Needs Always Remember That

This Meditation Hall begins, I hope you bring all your spirit to meditate. Please develop a strong mind to meditate. Always remember to meditate, remember how to escape birth and death, and forget to eat and drink to meditate. If you are not enlightened, you will not stop. You should have a vow as strong as a diamond.

If someone scolds you, pretend you didn't hear them. If someone beats you, you feel like you don't feel anything. I don't know whether to eat or not, I don't know whether to sleep or not. If you achieve such a state, you will immediately know that the efforts and things you did in the past are just superficial. Only today will you truly understand how to meditate.

At the beginning of the Meditation Hall, I will say a few crude and simple sentences to you, but if you understand them, they will be of great benefit. If you don't understand, it will help a lot. Someone asked: how does it help? I can't tell you now because once you understand, obstacles will arise and you won't be able to progress. Now I say a few words, I hope you will pay attention. The four verses are as follows:

Sanskrit meditation na paramita

Try to practice pure meditation and enter into greed

The high mountains and deep waters are fearless

Water penetrates beyond the natural world.

Meditation in Sanskrit is called Zen paramita. If this method is practiced to perfection, it will take us to the other side of the ocean of suffering. In Chinese, it is translated as meditation, also known as thought-thinking tu (practice of thinking). However, if you want to study it meticulously, you need to penetrate it deeply. What is insight? It's greed! Insight into the sentence "Who is Buddha's name." No matter how high the mountains are or how deep the sea is, I am not afraid. Only then did I realize that outside this sky, there were other endlessly overlapping skies. Therefore, we have to constantly contemplate, that is, look at the sentence " Who is Buddha's name." Look again and again at that sentence until the mountains and waters are completely free of doubt, that is, until we think that the mountains have ended, the rivers have ended, there is no more place to go, then when we return to nature, we will see the willow hidden in the flowers allied to the village, meaning we will see a village with flowers in the willow tree.

(Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas,

July 31, 1983)

Why Is It Not Compatible With The Way?

"The reason Sentient Beings cannot attain the true Way is because they have false and deluded minds. When you have a deceitful mind, it will shock the gods. When the spirit is shocked, we will be attached to all things. When we are attached to all things, we give birth to greed. When you are greedy, trouble will arise. Defilements and delusions make the body and mind suffer. That's why we fall into impurity, wander in samsara, sink into the sea of ​​suffering and forever lose the true path. The true path is eternal, the enlightened person attains it himself. Once you have attained enlightenment, you will always be pure."

Why is it that no matter how hard we work, we can't correspond with the Tao and can't move forward? What is the reason? Just because I still have a mind that is false, false and not real. I also like things that are far away, seek fame and gain. That means empty minds. If you have a false mind, there will still be fluctuations in your self-nature. For example, a bucket of water, when not stirred, all the sand and mud will settle to the bottom and the water surface will become pure. If you use a stick to stir the water, it will become dirty. That stick is likened to a false mind. From then on, I cannot distinguish between what is fake and what is real, and cannot distinguish between good and evil. At that time, the eyes to see the truth (Trach Phap Eye) will not be enough and wisdom will not appear. When the impure water is not pure, we will be attached to all things, our mind will be confused, and we will not be able to find the path to liberation. Why is that? Because we are attached to all things, we will give birth to the mind of greed, thinking that all things are real. When you give birth to a greedy mind and desire, you will create troubles for yourself. When we are greedy and do not get what we want, afflictions arise. If we desire to get it, it also gives rise to afflictions, because afflictions and delusions are closely linked together. Therefore, we are submerged in the water of the five desires of this evil realm of five impurities and cannot restore our pure nature. Therefore, one is born and then dies, and dies and then is born again; Birth and death are endless and never end. When you are born, you don't know why you were born, so you are confused. When I die, I don't know why I died, and I'm confused. Not only is he confused at birth, but he is also confused at death. Even at birth, you are confused all your life, not knowing anything clearly. Therefore, in the cycle of birth and death, we lose our true mind. Once our true mind is lost, we dive into the sea of ​​suffering, unable to rise up, unable to swim out. If we understand this principle, we will be enlightened, not be swayed by false realms, but wisdom will always be present. When you have wisdom, you will no longer be crazy.

The Shurangama Sutra says: " When the crazy mind is cut down, that is Bodhi. " When the crazy mind is destroyed, that cessation is enlightenment. Why is it not compatible with the Tao? It's because the crazy mind has never stopped. This crazy mind is also the mind that is dissatisfied with reality, it is also the heart of bottomless greed, it is also the heart of love and jealousy. If you can get rid of this mind, then it is wisdom, it is also enlightenment, it is also the essence of Buddha nature. However, everyone forgets this principle, thus becoming confused. In the realm of ignorance, people think that they are happy, joyful, and joyful, and then do not find a way to escape the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death of the Three Realms.

tieu_de: Be Careful When Preaching the Sutras and Preaching the Dharma
tom_tat: Regardless of whether you are a monk or a lay person, when preaching the sutras and preaching the Dharma, you need to be very careful. Before preaching the sutra, you must sit quietly for five minutes, calm your mind, then open the sutra book and clasp your hands with all your strength...
noi_dung:
Be Careful When Preaching the Sutras and Preaching the Dharma

Regardless of whether you are a monk or a lay person, when preaching the sutras and preaching the Dharma, you need to be very careful. Before preaching the sutra, you must sit quietly for five minutes, calm your mind, then open the sutra book, clasp your hands in utmost reverence, read and recite the sutra text once, and then explain the meaning in detail. If you don't understand the sutras and just forcefully explain them, it won't make sense. Therefore, when preaching the Sutra or preaching the Dharma, we must first clearly understand the name and appearance of the Dharma Sutra. First of all, we must study the scriptures and their meaning clearly, otherwise it is easy to explain incorrectly. But if you miss one inch, you will go a mile, making people who listen to the sutra unable to comprehend it, and even feel confused and difficult to understand.

People who study Buddhism should not be greedy for speed, because the food you swallow will not know its taste, meaning you need to eat slowly and chew slowly to know the taste of the food. Eating too much and not chewing thoroughly will only harm you. When preaching the sutras, pay attention to the meaning of the sutras, because if you preach incorrectly, not only will you not gain any merit, but you will also create more sins. There is a saying: "According to the text's interpretation, the Buddha's three times are unfair, if they separate the sutra from one word, that is the same theory, " means that according to the text, the interpretation is unjust to the three Buddhas, if one word is left out of the sutra, it is a ghost speaking. The consequences are very serious, so be careful.

For those who listen to the sutra, they must also try their best to listen attentively. Regardless of whether monks, nuns or Lay Buddhists preach sutras or dharma, if they preach well, you should still pay attention and listen. If they preach poorly, you should pay more attention. We have to research where we preach well and where we preach poorly. If you preach well, you must learn, if you preach poorly, you must find a way to correct it, because it is a mirror for you to look at yourself. Only with such an attitude can we train our eyes to find the truth, called Trach Phap Nhan.

Trach Phap Nhan or the eye that sees the truth comes from cultivating precepts, cultivating concentration, cultivating wisdom, these three aspects. If the precepts of concentration and wisdom are fully integrated without hindrance, then you will naturally understand all the scriptures without the slightest obstacle. At that time, when preaching the sutras and preaching the Dharma, the words and words flowed out endlessly. Ancient people preached sutras, some preached to the point that flowers fell from the sky and golden lotus rose from the ground. Even though you have not reached such a state yet, you still need to mock and preach without hindrances and preach the sutras without hindrances.

(Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, August 11, 1983)

tieu_de: Learning from the Example of a Wise Person is a Brave One
tom_tat: Meaning: When you see a good person, think of a way to be like them and you will be a brave person. We must imitate the behavior of sages to set an example for ourselves. What is a gentle person? A good person is a virtuous person. Whenever I meet…
noi_dung:
Learn from the Example of a Wise Person to Be a Brave One

Today's couplet is:

"A wise man is proud of a brave warrior."

Meaning: When you see a good person, think of a way to be like them and you will be a brave person. We must imitate the behavior of sages to set an example for ourselves. What is a gentle person? A good person is a virtuous person. Whenever we meet a wise person, we must do our best to be as good as that person. We have to learn and follow their example, we need to have ethics, manners, and education like them. Don't just think and let it go, but actually practice and make an effort to learn. Every gesture and action of that person must be considered as a model. If you don't learn and just keep thinking, it's of no use. We must truly learn to be a brave warrior, a hero, and a great magician.

A brave man is not a fool. What is stupidity? Simply put, dull means stupid. Someone said: "He is a gentle person! (The word sage in Chinese has the same sound as the word salty.) Then he just keeps being a gentle person, it has nothing to do with me. He wants to be a "salty person,", then I want to be a salty person." People who are salty or salty don't care, good or bad are not good at all, they are just people who are full and waiting to die. Once they die, it's over. That is the thought of a lazy person, who will never be able to raise his head.

(Vo Ngon Duong,

August 13, 1983)

tieu_de: The Six Great Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas
tom_tat: Those of you who are far away, the good and knowledgeable people who are near are coming! Today, let's study together how to be human and become Buddha. The way to be a human being must be based on the eight virtues of filial piety, kindness, loyalty, trust, propriety, righteousness, integrity, etc.
noi_dung:
Six Great Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas

Those of you who are far away, the good and knowledgeable people who are near are coming! Today, let's study together how to be human and become Buddha. The way to be human must be based on the eight virtues of filial piety, kindness, loyalty, trust, politeness, righteousness, integrity, and shame as standards. If you want to become a Buddha, you must expand the scope of these eight virtues, be filial to the whole world, be in harmony with the whole world, be loyal to the whole world, be faithful to the whole world; even virtue, righteousness, politeness, wisdom and courage to the whole world. We must use the spirit of openness and tolerance, "older children without outside, younger children without internal" to practice Buddha Dharma; However, it is not easy to reach the ultimate goodness and beauty of this spirit.

Currently, many practitioners feel that practicing Buddhism is like losing something. Why is it said that " is like losing something?" Because there is no benefit for them to grasp or enjoy, they feel like they are at a loss or disadvantage; Because of that, they become sluggish, depressed, and no longer enthusiastic about cultivating. Dear friends, please pay attention!

Letting go will never die, exchange will never be born;

Let go of the false impermanence and become the true imperishable one.

(If you cannot let go of death, you cannot exchange life;

If you can't let go of the fake, you won't be able to achieve the real!)

We should open our eyes and be liberal in our thinking; Don't just know about yourself, your family, or your country. We need to make our minds as large as space, covering the entire Dharma Realm, and think about the benefits of all humanity, not just calculating the pros and cons for ourselves!

For humanity, there is only benefit, not harm, which is the basis of cultivating the Way. How to benefit humanity? How not to harm the human body? Must practice the Six Great Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas:

First, No Fighting. We do not dispute with anyone. If you compete with me, I will not compete with you; you scold me, I don't scold you; you hit me, I don't hit you; You bully me, I don't bully you. That is the Principles from the past until now of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

In ancient times, when Buddha Shakyamuni was an immortal who practiced patience, he did not dispute with King Ca Loi but only used virtue to inspire that king. After cutting off the immortal's limbs, King Ca Loi asked: "Are you angry?"

Fairy Nhan Nhuc replied: "No! I'm not angry!"

King Ca Loi did not believe it, so he asked again: "What do you use to prove that you have no anger?"

The immortal said: "If I truly do not have anger, my hands and feet will immediately grow back!" After saying that, his hands and feet indeed grew back, as normal as before.
