Not only did the immortal have no anger, but he also had great compassion, telling King Ca Loi: "In the future, when I become a Buddha, I will first convert the king to become a monk and practice the Way." Later, the immortal became a Buddha, that is, Buddha Shakyamuni. Based on his ancient vows, he went to Deer Park to convert Venerable Kieu Tran Nhu (descendant of King Ca Loi) to become a monk and became one of the first five Bhikkhus.

Second, No Greed. If the greedy mind rebels, it is truly bottomless greed, whether it is greed for money or material things, it always feels like it is not enough. The more greedy you are, the more inadequate you feel. The more you feel inadequate, the more greedy you become. Greedy until old age still hasn't awakened! People are harmed by this word "tham" all their lives, until death they still feel that they do not own this or that thing, so they feel extremely regretful. How pitiful it is! The second principle of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is not to be greedy for any money, benefits, or good reputation, in short, not to be greedy for anything; Each person only follows their duty to propagate Buddha Dharma and continue the Buddha's wisdom!

When the Buddha was still alive, one day when he and Venerable Ananda were walking, along the way they came across a pile of gold. Buddha didn't look at that pile of gold, just kept going. Venerable Ananda, because his concentration had not yet reached "fire monkey", he looked one more time before leaving. Buddha said to Ananda: "That is a poisonous snake!"

At that time, a farmer working in the fields nearby heard about poisonous snakes and immediately came to see what he thought was a pile of gold! So he happily brought that pile of gold home and immediately became a rich man. The neighbors were skeptical, not knowing how the farmer had so much money, so they reported it to the King. The king immediately sent people to arrest the farmer to question the reason for his sudden wealth. The farmer then honestly told his story clearly.

The king even sent people to search the farmer's house. Discovering that there was a lot of gold in the house, they immediately confiscated it all and presented it to the King. Seeing the gold, the King immediately became angry, because that gold was stolen from the national treasury. Because he thought the farmer was a robber, the King ordered him to be imprisoned in a dungeon. Only then did the farmer suddenly understand why the Buddha said that pile of gold was a poisonous snake. This event proves that we should not be greedy for wealth that comes unexpectedly!

Third, Don't Pray. The policy of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is not to dispel fate, not to seek fate, and not to transform fate. "Request" and "Greed" are not much different. Greed is something that exists but something that is not, not yet manifested into action; while praying is a practical desire, wherever you go, you entice, hook up, and use every trick to achieve what you ask for. What do you pray for? Pray for money, pray for material things, in general pray for all benefits.

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas prays inwards, not outwards. "Inner search for the mind" means looking inward to eliminate all confusion, delusion, imagination, wildness, jealousy, obstacles, greed, anger, and ignorance in one's mind. Don't decorate or paint outwards, just make the inside pure and dignified, that's enough. Someone said:

Humanity has no need for a proud Chapter.

(When people reach the place they do not want, the Chapter naturally becomes noble.)

If we do not beg for anything from others, our Chapter will naturally become noble, without impure thoughts.

When the Buddha was still alive, there was a poor couple who not only had no land to work on but also had little food to eat. They lived in a cave and both of them had only one cloth to cover, so whoever went out to beg for food wore that cloth. It's not said to what extent they are poor, but you probably understand. One day, a Bich Chi Buddha wanted to test whether the couple had a greedy heart or not, so he went to their cave to create love. The couple discussed how to make offerings to this monk. They really had nothing to offer, so they offered that single piece of cloth. However, they do not wish for anything, only sincerely making offerings to the monks.

This Pratyekabuddha immediately brought that cloth to make offerings to the Buddha. Buddha Shakyamuni clearly knew the origin of the cloth, so he told the story to the crowd in the Dharma Assembly, and at the same time praised the merits of the benefactor who donated the cloth. At that time, the King was also present at the Dharma Assembly. When he learned about this, the King felt extremely ashamed. He did not expect that even in the country he ruled, there were such poor people; So he immediately sent a minister to bring food and clothes to give to the poor couple, while also providing them with accommodation and finding jobs. That couple did not have the heart to wish for it and yet they received such retribution. It is truly true that giving up one thing will result in countless retributions!

Fourth, Not Selfish. Why has the world deteriorated to the level it is today? Because people are too selfish, when it comes to things that are beneficial to them, they compete to do them, and when it comes to things that are not beneficial to them, they indifferently sit with their arms folded and watch, or calmly talk casually with the mood of "standing on the other side watching the fire burn!"

There are many things about selfishness: selfishness about status, selfishness about honor, selfishness about rights, selfishness about money... In general, everything is caused by selfishness. Because of selfishness, I don't think about others and only care about myself. There is a saying:

Ma ha tát bất quản tha,

Amitabha Buddha and his ancestors.

(Bậc Ma Ha Tát không nghĩ đến người khác,

Amitabha Buddha, everyone is concerned.)

That's a joke with Hinayana ideology. Confucianism also said:

The names of the Tao Mon pre-snow characters,

Mac governs others in the mist.

(Snow in front of your house, sweep it yourself, Don't worry about the frost on your roof!)

That is the behavior of not meddling in other people's affairs. As humans on earth, we must help each other and guide each other. Therefore, everyone should promote Mahayana thought, study the Bodhisattva spirit, come to rescue when they hear suffering, and should not be happy in the face of other people's misfortunes! If people are not selfish, they can live together in harmony like a family. It is because of selfishness that many problems arise. Therefore, Selflessness is the fourth Principle of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

Fifth, Do not benefit yourself. This Principles is even more important than the fourth Principles. Everyone wants to benefit themselves; However, we definitely do not benefit ourselves because only then can the world become better. "Not benefiting yourself" means wanting to benefit others, forgetting about yourself. This spirit of "selfishness and selflessness" (forgetting oneself for others) also surpasses the actions of Bodhisattvas because Bodhisattvas self-benefit others, self-savage others, self-enlighten others, not only benefit others, only save others and only enlighten others!

Friday, No Echoes. Not lying means not intentionally deceiving others. Why do people lie? It is because of fear of losing profits, fear of loss, that people find ways to lie! If you always treat everyone with sincerity, you will naturally keep this sixth Principle of No False Speech.

Many people hear about these Six Great Principles and feel very uncomfortable and unhappy. If someone is unhappy or doesn't accept me, I don't accept it. I want to make it clear to everyone: I have never opposed anything in the world. Why is that? Because my Principles are "Everything's OK" everything is OK. However, if someone opposes me, I welcome it and absolutely will not refute it!

Today I will only briefly present to you the Six Great Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas; If you want to say it completely, you will never be able to say it all. If you apply these Six Principles to yourself, it will be extremely beneficial for you!

(August 14, 1983)

Practitioners cannot attain Phan Duyen

My principles are:

The group of children has no fate,

The hungry death does not ask for fate,

With the same destiny of death,

Depending on fate, there is no change, there is no change in fate

Safeguarding the self of the Three Great Principles.

Giving up one's life for the sake of Buddhism,

Create a network for your duty,

Right Livelihood for Sangha,

That means reason, reason means truth,

The Patriarch's heart and soul transmission.

Means:

Despite the cold and death, there is no fate;

Even if you starve to death, don't beg;

Even if you die poor, don't ask for help.

Depends on fate, does not change; constant, depending on fate;

Those three Principles, we must preserve.

Sacrifice yourself for Buddhist cause,

Create a network for your duty,

Right Livelihood for Enrichment.

Understand things, understand reason; clear reason, understand things;

Circulates the Patriarch's sect's lineage.

That is our duty, we hope everyone will make every effort to fulfill it.

Practitioners should not have a mind that is predestined, but should have a pure mind, neither greedy nor contaminated. I often tell you that anyone who has left home to practice, with one heart in pursuit of the Way, does not need anything, is not greedy for anything, even a blade of grass cannot be arbitrarily asked for it and cannot be arbitrarily given to others. There is a sentence:

One world cannot help but be cruel,

The world has no choice but to protect its people.

(Not even a mustard seed should be given to others,

Not even a mustard seed should be taken from a person.)

As for "destiny, " needs to be clearly distinguished and must make this "destiny" become pure, untainted. Pure fate means not having a greedy mind; contaminated condition means having a greedy mind. Monastic people can receive offerings; However, do not be greedy for offerings, do not plot offerings, only then will you be a true disciple of the Buddha.

If you are inherently worthy of receiving offerings but do not accept them, that is true character, because you did not become a monk for the sake of food and clothing. What's the use of enjoying beautiful clothes and delicious food but not practicing properly? As for things outside the body, you should look down on them and not take them seriously. There should be a sentence:

A gentleman plans the Way, not reality. (A gentleman seeks the Way, not food or drink.) Now we can change that sentence to: A gentleman is in poverty,

Achieving humanity and knowing life.

(A gentleman is content with poverty,

Those who understand life's stories know how to settle down.)

Monastics need to understand that before the Dharma karma has been accomplished, they cannot be in debt. If you are in debt, you will be bound and cannot be freed. Especially with impure conditions, they can harm you to the point of "pulling out the vacuum, " not achieving freedom. However, most monastics like to be offered offerings and like to receive gifts from others. Once bound by impure conditions, it is not easy to escape from the Three Realms. "The string" of contaminated fate is tightly wrapped around you, there is no way to remove it. Therefore, to avoid all trouble, you should not be attached to things that are not true or pure!

Monastics are divided into seven classes:

The first type of monastic person has " a light and light body, " and has nothing at all.

One dust is not contaminated, ten thousand conditions are empty.

(Not even a speck of dust sticks, all causes and conditions are empty.)

The second class of monks carries a cloth bag in their hand; Outsiders cannot know what is in the bag.

The third class of monastics carries the burden on their shoulders. Because they cannot let go, they carry all their assets with them wherever they go. Even though they have to bear a heavy burden (sometimes weighing up to hundreds of pounds), they are willing. This country is not burdened, but using a backpack doesn't mean much!

The fourth class of monastics brings their belongings by car.

The fifth class of monastics brings their belongings by train.

The sixth class of monastics brings their belongings by ship.

The seventh class of monastics brings their belongings by plane.

Those are common shortcomings that monastics often have.

I hope that those who follow me to become monks will soon attain Buddhahood; If you cannot become a Buddha, you must also become a Bodhisattva. In short, we need to benefit others, not ourselves. Do not arbitrarily take Thuong Tru's things and give them to others. You may think there is merit, but in reality, it is stealing things from the Sangha! Befriending others, arbitrarily giving away personal benefits, taking public property to use for private purposes, is an act of sabotaging Bodhimanda's rules. Anyone who commits such acts must quickly correct them and not repeat them; If not, then be careful!

(August 15, 1983)

tieu_de: Open the Five Eyes to See the Real Dragon
tom_tat: What does a dragon really look like? Except for the saints who have opened the Five Eyes, most people do not know the true face of the dragon. In China, people often draw dragons with a horned head, scaly body, bulging eyes, mouth...
noi_dung:
Open the Five Eyes to See the Real Dragon

What does a dragon really look like? Except for the saints who have opened the Five Eyes, most people do not know the true face of the dragon. In China, people often draw dragons with a horned head, a scaly body, bulging eyes, a large mouth, a mustache, four legs, a very long body, and a very short tail. People who draw dragons only draw the dragon's head without drawing the dragon's tail to represent mystical drawing, because:

The divine dragon's hands do not show its tail.

(The magical dragon sees the head but does not see the tail.)

Why do Chinese people draw dragons like that? Because there was a Zen Master who, while meditating, saw the appearance of a dragon like that. Dragons have magical powers, unpredictable changes, can change big and small, sometimes hide and sometimes appear. The Great Master of the Sixth Patriarch once used his rice bowl to subdue a large dragon and eliminate disasters for Nam-Hoa Temple.

Dragon is a big insect, because in the past, when practicing, he was "Superior" (quickly returned to practice Mahayana), so he had supernatural powers, but he was "Procrastination" (slow, not diligent in the Precepts), so he was reborn as an animal. There are many different types of dragons, kim-dragon (yellow dragon), bai-dragon (white dragon), qing-dragon (green dragon) and hac-dragon (black dragon). Dragons can be born from fetuses, from eggs, from humidity, or from transformation. There are also Cau-long (horned dragon), eagle-dragon, Giao-long (thuong luong), ly-long (black dragon); heavenly-long, earth-long, king-long, human-long; and there are also mermaid-turned-dragon (dragon transformed into a fish), code-turned-dragon (dragon transformed into a horse), statue-turned-dragon (dragon transformed into an elephant), and hap-turned-long (dragon transformed into a toad).

Dragons must endure four types of suffering:

Suffering from being eaten by a golden eagle (suffering from being eaten by a golden eagle);

The dragon transforms into a snake (when having sex, the dragon turns into a snake, and this transformation is extremely painful and miserable);

Suffering from small insects hidden in dragon scales (suffering from being bitten and sucked by blood by small insects hidden in dragon scales);

The heat causes the body to suffer (when the sun is hot, the sand stuck in the dragon's scales are heated by the sunlight, causing the dragon to itch and feel very miserable).

The dragon's mission is "to spread clouds and rain, " to spread clouds and make rain. However, there are five cases where dragons cannot make rain.

The fire element increases in strength (the element "fire" increases strongly);

The wind blows and scatters (the wind blows away the clouds);

Asura collect clouds into the sea (A-tu-la species collect clouds into the sea);

Vu guru is loose (rain god is loose);

Sentient Beings' karma is heavy.

Do you want to know what a dragon looks like? Then, you need to make an effort to practice and meditate; When the Five Eyes open, you will see the original face of the real dragon. Now I will tell you a koan about dragons. This is a story that happened to me, completely true, absolutely not a fabrication.

When I was in the Northeast, I accepted a disciple named Qua Thuan. He practiced very diligently and in less than half a year was able to sit in Zen and enter Concentration. While entering Concentration, he can know the principle of Cause and Effect, cyclical retribution; His meticulous practice seems to be almost there. Later, he went out and built a thatched house as a place to practice. The day the cottage was finished, he invited me to clear the land. I and four other disciples went there

(Of those four people, two people have opened the Five Eyes). At that time, I didn't notice that next to the cottage there was a Dragon-king temple.

That day something happened: when we were about to meditate, two disciples who had opened the Five Eyes came and said to me: "Master! Ten dragons came to ask for refuge from Master, and are still waiting outside the cottage!"

I told the disciples: "You must not talk nonsense! How do you know they are dragons? Why do they take refuge in me? How can I be their Master? I don't have strong skills like them!"

They said: "They call themselves dragons, and are now kneeling outside, definitely asking for refuge to Master."

It was summer, there was a drought, there was no rain, the rice seedlings in the field were almost dry. I just told those dragons (turned into humans): "You can take refuge in me if you want, but I have one condition. You are dragons, specializing in making rain, and currently the Hebin area has not had rain for a long time so it is extremely dry. If it rains tomorrow, the day after tomorrow I will give you Refuge; If not, I won't accept you as disciples!"

They answered in unison: "Dear Teacher! It is true that our mission is to make rain; But without the Jade Emperor's order, we do not dare to make it rain, because if we disobey the order, we will be punished."

I said: "Go before the Jade Emperor and say: 'In Hebin, there is a monk who requests that rain be brought down within forty miles of Herbin.'That is my condition."

The next day it rained heavily and the drought ended. Everywhere within forty miles of Hebin received showers. The next day, I gave those ten dragons Refuge and gave them the common Dharma name of Level Tu. After taking refuge, those dragons disappear and are no longer seen.

They have transformed their fellow humans.

From then on, no matter where I went, there was water to use! When I went to Hong Kong, Hong Kong had water; When I arrived at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas also had water. It was not a miracle that appeared, but because these ten dragons and their relatives protected the Dharma.

Someone asked: "Master! Master saw what shape those ten dragons looked like?"

When they came to take refuge with me, those dragons transformed into humans, just like ordinary people, with no difference at all; Only people who have opened the Five Eyes will know that it is a dragon. Do you want to know what dragons are like? Then, quickly put effort into cultivating the Way, meditate diligently, reduce false thoughts, don't get angry, and regardless of whether you encounter adversity or favorable circumstances, be patient and don't become attached. When reaching the realm of "unborn thought, untainted object" (not even a single thought is born, not even a speck of dust sticks), then the Five Eyes will naturally open. Then, you will see the dragon's face clearly!

Human Life Is Like a Dream, Wake Up!

In this world, people let go of the truth to hold on to the false, thus forever turning their backs on enlightenment to harmonize with the dust of the world, falling into the dream of birth and death. To be born drunk means that while living, one is like a drunk person, not knowing where one came from. Dream death means that when you die, you will be like someone dreaming, not knowing where they will go. Everyone lives in a dream. Taking the fake as real, greedy for fame and profit, greed never stops.

In your dream, you see yourself working as an official, or making money, or having status, rights, honor, or having a beautiful wife and concubines, a house full of children, honor and wealth, and an endless life. Suppose in that dream someone said to you: "Grandpa! This is just an illusion, it's not real, " you will never believe. Wait until you wake up and no one will tell you that you had a dream, you also know clearly that you just had a dream.

Last night I dreamed of poinsettia beans, becoming a prime minister, becoming an emperor, becoming a god, extremely happy. Woke up today: "Oh! It's all just a dream of spring!" (dream of spring means a very short dream). That is awareness. If you don't wake up and choose the dream as real, you will be attached, not let go, attached to confusion, and will never be enlightened. Right now I'm dreaming in the middle of the day but haven't awakened yet, so I live confused, and then I die confused. Where did you come from when you were born here? Where will I go when I die? Don't know! All my life I never woke up. Think about it, what does that mean? What do I have to remember? Is there anything worth not giving up everything?

All my life I have been bound so tightly by the rope of the three poisons and the five desires that I have no freedom to transform myself, let alone liberation. Therefore, you must develop the mind to become a monk and practice the Way, meditate diligently, and make an effort to bow to the Buddha, that is, you will untie the rope of the three poisons and the five desires, and eventually one day you will be completely liberated. At that time, I will wake up and look back to see that the things I have done in the past were completely like an illusion, all of which were not the truth. Now that I have awakened, I can escape the cycle of the three worlds, no longer limited by birth and death, free to be born when I want to be born, free to die when I want to die, free to come and go as I please. That is true liberation, that is: "The Great Dream of Initial Awakening".

Usually we hold on to the false and lies and forget the truth. What is falsehood? It is the joy and happiness of the five desires: talent, form, name, and food. What is truth? That is, the happiness of Nirvana lies in the four virtues: permanent, happy, self, and pure. However, people are very strange. When the truth is lost, they are not afraid, but when the false thing is lost, they are extremely afraid. Why is that? Because everyone in this world accepts the enemy as their child, abandons the roots and follows the tree, takes the false as real, does not awaken, therefore remains in dreams, attached to the dream realm.

Because of causes and conditions, confusion arises, creating evil karma and then receiving retribution, like a speck of dust flying in the air, unable to control oneself. That dust particle, depending on karma, circulates in the six paths of samsara without ever stopping. Therefore, it is said: "If you cannot destroy the gate of fame and fortune, you will not be able to escape the cycle of reincarnation, " means that if you cannot destroy the gate of fame and fortune, you will not be able to escape the cycle of reincarnation. As long as you are not moved by the realm, then you will escape the six paths of reincarnation.

(August 21, 1983)

What is "The Five Existing Generals"

When you have done many good deeds and have enough merit, you will be born in heaven and enjoy pleasure. Gods and people are often in concentration. They take the pleasure of meditation as food, have the pleasure of the fullness of the Dharma, but that pleasure is not the end. By the time they have enjoyed all the heavenly blessings, they will naturally fall into reincarnation and suffer the retribution for what they did in the past.

The blessing of the gods is that whenever you think about clothes, clothes come immediately. When you think about eating and drinking, eating and drinking come immediately. Their clothes are very light, only three pieces (twenty-four pieces are one tael), which means they are very light, so it is said: "Thien robe is unfit," means that the clothes do not need to be sewn or cut at all. No matter how big or small, you want it to fit snugly, not too big and not too small. Whenever you want to eat or drink something, the Chapter will immediately appear in front of you, not too much or too little, making the eater satisfied.

When the gods are about to die, five signs of decay appear:

First: The withered mandarin flower (withered flower hat): the gods have flower hats, extremely dignified, never withering. But when it was time to die, that flower hat naturally withered.

Second: Dirty clothes (dirty clothes): the gods wear clothes that are not only beautiful and pure, but also don't have a speck of dust on them, and don't need to be washed at all. When they were about to die, their clothes suddenly became dirty and dust stuck to them.

Third: The lower ejaculate appears (armpit sweating): the body of the gods never sweats. But when he was about to die, sweat appeared under his armpits.

Fourth: The body is unclean (the body has a foul smell): the gods have previously practiced very righteously and strictly maintained the precepts, so they have the fragrance of precepts (incense produced by the precepts), often emitting a fragrant scent. Why does our body smell bad? It's because we don't keep the precepts. When I'm dying, my body gives off the smell of death.

Fifth: Not happy with the seat (not liking where one sits): the gods are always in concentration, always as if motionless, always clear. But when the four signs of decay appeared, the gods saw it and knew they were about to die, so their minds were scattered, delusions arose, they couldn't sit still, they couldn't stand still, they stood then sat again, sat then stood again, turned around a few times, then stopped breathing. When they die, they are reincarnated into the six paths of reincarnation. If their hell karma ripens, they will be born in hell; If the animal karma ripens, they will be reincarnated as an animal; If the Asura karma is ripe, they will be born in the Asura realm; If the human karma matures, they will be reincarnated into the human world. However, in each realm, there are many different angels, all kinds of different levels, for example, in the human realm, the highest is the emperor, the bottom is all the beggars, the middle level is all kinds of classes, some are rich and wealthy, some are poor and lowly, some are smart, some are stupid, some are long-lived, some are young, some are healthy, some are sick, all are influenced by karma. feel it.

tieu_de: In the Ashram, you must be careful in what you say and do
tom_tat: Anyone who comes to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must be careful in their words and actions, and must let go of their greed for fame and profit. Don't look down on people, think you're the best, better than...
noi_dung:
In the Ashram You Must Be Careful About Your Words and Deeds

Anyone who comes to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must be careful in their words and actions, and must let go of their greed for fame and profit. You should not look down on people, think that you are the best, the best, then put yourself on high and despise others. That is an act of high tribute and arrogance.

If there are impurities carried in the mind, or in the body, or in the spirit, how can one achieve spiritual karma? I often tell you:

True self-recognition

Discourse on other people's non-existence

Tha phi means self phi

Same name as Dai-Bi.

Please consider others as yourself. Consider the pleasure and joy of others as your own happiness. When others are suffering, consider it your own suffering. When someone does something good, we also compare it to ourselves doing it. When someone does something evil, we are also hurt and sad as if we did it ourselves. We must have such thoughts in order to be able to live happily with others, to encourage and help those who violate the precepts, as well as to encourage those who keep the precepts. We cannot have the mind " of jealousy, " means being jealous of good people and talented people, nor can we hinder others from developing the mind of bodhichitta.

After becoming a monk, you should work quickly at the temple, absolutely do not go around bragging or propagating your merits saying that I did this, I did that. If you brag about your merits, there is no merit at all. You should not imitate like people today, if you do a little you are afraid of being disadvantaged, if you do anything you are afraid of losing. He thinks he's very smart, but in reality he's stupid. You don't need to say all the things you do every day because the Dharma Protectors remember them very clearly. When merit is complete, there will be a natural response, so it is said: " naturally smells of fragrance, " means: if there is a scent, it is naturally fragrant, without the need for wind to blow it away.

Sentient Beings have the same mistake, that is, when doing work, they say that they should not have an ego (ie they should not do it). When it's time to eat, he says that he shouldn't have a human appearance (because there are no other people, so he can just eat as much as he wants). When it's time to argue with each other, say: "oh, we shouldn't have Sentient Beings!" (That is, just keep arguing, there are no Sentient Beings). When it comes time to eat meat, you think that there is no false feeling (that is, the piece of meat has no life at all, just keep eating!). Even without shame, he said: "I eat you guys so that I can transcend you to the Western Heaven." Anyone who thinks like that and thinks they are smart is actually being deceived by their intelligence, and they will suffer a disadvantage, without even knowing it.

We practitioners must always control ourselves, must master and control all our movements, walk, stand, lie down, and do not leave the house (that is, the true mind). Not leaving means not looking for other people's mistakes, nor saying bad things about others, which means you have to be careful in your words and actions. Always reflect back the light, illuminate your heart, you must look for yourself, you must eliminate your strange impatience to preserve the practice of patience. Saying it over and over again, the main idea is that you should talk less, practice more, never brag about yourself, I'm like this, I'm like that. Now that you have become a monk, you should not have the same habits as a lay person. Why become a monk? Please reflect, look at yourself, should you or shouldn't you?

tieu_de: People who cultivate the Way should not be selfish
tom_tat: From the 7th lunar month (i.e. Vu Lan festival) until the 30th day of the 7th month (i.e. the birthday of Ksitigarbha), we organize two Ksitigarbha ceremonies to save the ghosts and ghosts to be reborn, and pray for world peace. That is…
noi_dung:
Dharma Cultivators Shouldn't Be Selfish

Today is the starting day of Ksitigarbha. Every year on the day

From the 7th lunar month (i.e. Vu Lan festival) until the 30th day of the 7th month (i.e. the birthday of Ksitigarbha), we organize two Ksitigarbha ceremonies to save the ghosts and ghosts to be reborn, and pray for world peace. That is the responsibility that the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must wholeheartedly carry out.

I hope that you will concentrate and single-mindedly recite "Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva," until your mind and mouth match, then you will definitely be inspired. You cannot do two things with one mind, you must concentrate your mind to chant His name. If we are not sincere and sincere, then although it cannot be said that there is no merit, the merit is not much. If we concentrate single-mindedly on reciting, then we will harmonize with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and when reciting to the point of "not reciting like self-reciting" (the mouth does not reciting but the mind always reciting), then in the heart, naturally pure and free, all afflictions will disappear.

People who practice religion should not be selfish, should not have the mindset of "nostalgia for children and delusional states." Whenever you get delicious food, give it to the masses to eat; Whenever there are beautiful clothes, they will be given to the public to wear; Whenever there is a safe place to live, it will be given to the public; If you have any good inspiration, please share it with the public and make offerings to everyone. Whatever merit I have, I should definitely give Dedication of Merit to Sentient Beings in the Dharma-world. If that doesn't work then I'm still selfish.

Anyone who has a good response should make offerings to everyone. Anyone who does not have a good response should tell everyone clearly. Don't put gold on your face (bragging about yourself), saying that I have beautiful touch like this, good like that. It's also not okay to hide it carefully and not tell others if you have a magical or miraculous inspiration. If you have such thoughts, you are selfish. Now everyone should reflect and see if they have fulfilled their responsibilities? Is it because we refuse to work, each person keeps pushing the other, I push him, he pushes me, no one is willing to shoulder his responsibilities.

Each of us must develop our minds and consider Buddhism as our own responsibility. Everyone must be responsible for the rise and fall of the Tao. It cannot be said: that is someone else's business, it has nothing to do with me.

For the sake of Buddhism, we must sacrifice everything, even if our bones are broken and our flesh is broken, we will not give up. One must have such a spirit to be a true follower of Buddhism. We should not take advantage of Buddhism to earn food or take advantage of Buddhism to have clothes and clothes, but we should do our best to support the Three Jewels. Only then will there be no selfishness.

You should not always be afraid of losses, always be afraid of disadvantages, always think of yourself as noble, think of yourself as the best. You must have the spirit of self-forgetfulness for the Dharma to be qualified to be a follower of Buddhism.

(August 25, 1983)

tieu_de: Following the example of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva
tom_tat: It means that hell is not yet empty, I swear I will not become a Buddha; After Sentient Beings have been saved, I have attained Bodhi. This spirit is truly compassionate. Bodhisattvas are extremely concerned and worried about us Sentient Beings, nothing...
noi_dung:
Imitate Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Example

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has the greatest vow power. He said:

"Hell is empty, vowing to never become a Buddha, Sentient Beings are brought to an end, and attain Bodhi."

It means that hell is not yet empty, I swear I will not become a Buddha; After Sentient Beings have been saved, I have attained Bodhi. This spirit is truly compassionate. Bodhisattvas are extremely concerned and worried about us Sentient Beings, there is nothing we can imagine. For Buddhists who strive to practice, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can appear and preach the Dharma while we are meditating or dreaming. Unfortunately, we do not understand the Bodhisattva's intention, and we betray His compassion. We are truly at fault with Him. However, the Bodhisattva did not get angry. He forgave the delusion of Sentient Beings, and continued to save Sentient Beings. When he saves all Sentient Beings, he will become a Buddha.

Bodhisattva's actions are all directed towards truth. Absolutely, He has no false intentions, even as small as a thread of silk, purely to save Sentient Beings from suffering and peace.

Currently we are celebrating Ksitigarbha, whoever has a true heart will be inspired, whoever has a sincere intention will benefit. Enjoying this is not about gaining magical powers, but about having your mind purified and free of delusions. When delusions end, we will have the realm of induction and communication. Someone said: "Peace is a feeling; knowing mistakes is also induction; Compared to before, I understand more clearly, it is also induction; Compared to before, I'm more diligent and effortless. That's also an induction." It's not wrong to say that, it's generally like that.

tieu_de: Accept Unreasonable Criticism
tom_tat: Now I would like to tell you my experience when I recited the Ksitigarbha Sutra. When I was seventeen years old, I started preaching the Six Patriarchs Dharma Jewel Platform Sutra and the Diamond Sutra to people. At first I didn't know…
noi_dung:
Accept Unreasonable Criticism

Now I would like to tell you my experience when I recited the Ksitigarbha Sutra. When I was seventeen years old, I started preaching the Six Patriarchs Dharma Jewel Platform Sutra and the Diamond Sutra to people. At first I didn't know how to preach but I still had to preach. Why is that? Because at that time there were many people who wanted to research and learn the classics but were illiterate. That's why I thought that I needed to take on this task, so I preached the sutras to them.

One day I accidentally discovered the Sutra of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows and I felt like I had caught something precious. Reading it once, I saw that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is extremely compassionate. He cares so much about us, but we don't know anything about it. Therefore, I made up my mind to kneel every day in front of the Buddha's temple and recite a set of Ksitigarbha Sutras. The floor of the Buddha Hall was tiled, there was no mattress, and I only wore regular cloth pants. Kneeling on the tile floor and reciting a set of Sutras takes two hours. I was so focused on chanting that my knees were bleeding without even feeling any pain. The more I chanted, the more comfortable my mind became. Every day, at the right time, I kneel in front of the Buddha's temple and sincerely chant. More than a hundred days later, demonic obstacles arose so I had to stop and could no longer recite.

If a person cultivates the Way, if he does not practice diligently, there will be no evil obstacles to test him. Whenever you get a little achievement, the devil will come and test you to see if you have concentration or not? While I was reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra, a Lay Buddhist came to the temple to make offerings. He saw me kneeling and chanting the Sutras, and he praised me very much, and told the people in the temple that he was so diligent, that he was so diligent... After this Lay Buddhist left, all the monks in the temple scolded me: "You pretend too well, trying to get Lay Buddhist's attention to show that you are a diligent practitioner. You're such an exploiter!" At that time I didn't argue at all, I understood myself, I only knew that I was chanting Sutras for the sake of practice. But from then on, absurd things often happened. Before chanting the sutras, the monks scolded me: "You fake practice."After chanting the sutras, the monks scolded me again: "Are you already pretending to practice!"Every day they scolded you loudly but I still endured without saying a word.

After I had been chanting for more than a hundred days, the demonic obstacles really came. One day, I had just finished reciting a set of Ksitigarbha Sutras when the senior brother came up to me and hit me. I don't understand why, and I don't dare ask why. Then he scolded me: "You are a useless person, here lazily enjoying your time. People have jobs out there, and I'm here pretending to chant sutras to perform for people to see. Is the temple not the place for you to practice like that? What merit do you have to practice here?" Therefore, I have no choice but to stop reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra.

Today, encountering Ksitigarbha Ksitigarbha made me remember the past. Practicing is not easy, but you can always encounter obstacles. You are very lucky to have met Bodhimanda who practiced very ideally, was not scolded, was not beaten, and was extremely leisurely and at ease. You all need to learn the example of patience, always strive in adversity, continue to practice diligently and practice diligently in all circumstances.

tieu_de: Advise Daughter-in-law to Be Filial to Her Parents-in-law
tom_tat: When I followed the Great Master Thuong Nhan of Tam Duyen Pagoda in Northeast China, one time because of the work of building the pagoda, I went out to the village to look for a truck to transport materials. About fifteen miles from the temple, there is a village...
noi_dung:
Advising Daughters-in-law to Be Filial to Their Parents-In-Law

When I followed the Great Master Thuong Nhan of Tam Duyen Pagoda in Northeast China, one time because of the work of building the pagoda, I went out to the village to look for a truck to transport materials. About fifteen miles from the pagoda, there is a village called Dai Ba. It was spring farming time so the farmers were very busy, so they couldn't find a car. I went to the village chief's house and he said: "We are very busy right now and don't have time to transport materials to the temple!" Just then, his sister-in-law came to see me and said: "Teacher! My child is sick and the doctor can't cure it. Can you show compassion and treat my child?"

I told her: "Because you are not filial to your parents-in-law, your child is sick. If you want your child to be cured of his illness, you must repent. She must bow before the ancestral tablet and pray that from now on she will be respectful to her husband's parents and live in harmony with everyone in the family. After that, she knelt before her parents-in-law to admit her mistake, and vowed not to make them sad again. If you are sincere like that, your child will definitely heal."

She immediately did as I said, but the child's illness still did not improve, so she immediately ran to see me. I said: "Please bring the child back to me." She immediately carried the child over, he was about three or four years old, his eyes were closed, his mouth was open. I used my hand to gently tap its head three times. Not long after that, the little boy suddenly opened his eyes, looked east and west. After about five minutes, he left his mother's hand and went down to the ground to run and play as quickly as usual.

At that time, the village chief was extremely happy and said to me: "Teacher! You saved my nephew from his illness. Tomorrow we will bring all the vehicles to the temple to help Master transport materials."

The next morning, he sent back nine cars for us to use. At night, while leaving, a donkey pulling a cart got crushed and broke its leg. The car owner was surprised and thought that if he worked for the temple, he must have merit, so why did he have such an accident. He thought for a long time but could not find the Cause and Effect of this incident, so he came and asked me: "Teacher! What kind of fate is this?"

I answered him: "You should not be restless or worried. Although the donkey's broken leg was damaged, it soon healed. This actually saved the lives of my family members."

He was very touched when he heard me say that and even decided to come the next day to help the temple carry materials.

From then on, whenever I went to any village to borrow a car to transport materials, everyone was happy to help because they knew that helping the pagoda would bring immeasurable merit. Some people even competed to lend a car or someone to help contribute to the pagoda.

(August 26, 1983)

tieu_de: The Thief Becomes a Filial Son
tom_tat: In my hometown in the Northeast, I once met a filial son named Vu named Chi Hue. In the past, he was a thief, snatched money, there was nothing evil that he wouldn't do. One day, he was seriously injured, from the point of death...
noi_dung:
The Thief Becomes a Pious Son

In my hometown in the Northeast, I once met a filial son named Vu named Chi Hue. In the past, he was a thief, snatched money, there was nothing evil that he wouldn't do. One day, he was seriously injured and came back to life from death. From then on, his conscience was awakened, he felt ashamed and determined to change his life and become a new person. He made a vow: "If I don't die, I will definitely go to my parents' grave to pay my respects." It didn't take long for his wound to heal. After returning home, he built a thatched hut near his parents' graves and stayed there for several years.

One year in the summer, it rained heavily and caused flooding. He started praying to the sky. If it stopped raining within three days, he would cut meat to sacrifice to heaven. He thought that if he waited for the rain to stop before offering sacrifices, it would be like a bribe, so he had to cut the meat right now to sacrifice to the heavens to show his sincerity and urgency. He immediately set up an incense burner and prayed to the heavens to protect the people in the area and make the crops good. After speaking, he immediately used a knife to cut a piece of meat right on his chest. At that moment, blood gushed out, causing him to faint on the ground.

His earnest sincerity touched heaven and earth, so a very miraculous reaction arose. Immediately the rain stopped and the sky cleared, and when his family brought him food to eat, they discovered he was lying on the ground, bleeding. They woke him up and treated him. After about half a month, the wound completely healed. During that time, there was a very cute bird that flew to his bed every day to comfort him and sing: "Da Tac Duc! Many virtues! Many are many good!" (meaning that doing much virtue, doing much virtue, much virtue is very good). That bird became his good friend. After half a month, I don't know where that bird flew to. Sincerity caused the rain to stop completely, and a magical bird came to be my friend. That realm was truly unbelievable.

One year, he and I met again, sat together for an hour, without saying a word to each other. Why is that? Because there's nothing worth talking about. Everything is expressed in silence " wordlessly, " he knows me, I also know him. When the mind shines, there is no need for words, only the intention can be understood, it cannot be expressed in words.

When I went to Taiwan to propagate the Dharma, I met Venerable Thuy Qua (aka Venerable Quang Kham). He and I were in the same situation, looking at each other without saying anything, but inside we were extremely happy. That is the induction effect of the soul, mind, mind, mind, mind, mind, mind, mind, mind, mind, mind, mind, mind, mind, mind and other people's mind being imprinted together; try to communicate, no more obstacles.

tieu_de: Four Essential Stages of Human Life
tom_tat: We all have to go through the four great sufferings of life called birth, old age, sickness and death, and no one can escape those four sufferings. Unless you practice the Way and escape the cycle of birth and death, there is no mention of...
noi_dung:
Four Essential Stages of Human Life

We all have to go through the four great sufferings of life called birth, old age, sickness and death, and no one can escape those four sufferings. Unless you cultivate the Way and escape the cycle of birth and death, there is nothing to talk about, most people in the world have to endure those four types of suffering.

When born, it is like being pressed down by two mountains, so when a child is born, the first thing he does is burst into tears, which shows suffering. Relatives who were confused by the situation came to congratulate him. Although it is a joy, is it actually a suffering? When you get old, your eyes become blurred, your ears become deaf, your teeth fall out, your hair turns gray, and your limbs stop moving as desired. It's extremely painful. When you get sick, the four elements are no longer in harmony and no longer cooperate with you. At that time, I was only bedridden, unable to stand up. Poverty and suffering go hand in hand, it is true that in suffering there is even more suffering. At that time, the mind wants a path, but the strength is not enough to follow it, do you think that is not suffering?

At the time of death, the suffering is indescribable, like a buffalo being stripped of its skin while alive, tearing out its intestines and liver for the sake of its children, being confused by the seven emotions and six desires, unable to let them go. In fact, death is something that everyone has to go through. So why is it that when we are born we are happy but when we die we are sad? Unfortunately, foolish and deluded people cannot break this attachment.

Now let's study the problem of where birth comes from, and where we die? If we understand this issue thoroughly, we can escape the three realms and no longer fall into samsara. In the past, Shakyamuni Buddha wanted to study this issue so he became a monk. He practiced asceticism for six years but could not achieve a method to solve the problem of birth and death. Finally, at the foot of the Bodhi tree, he sat in meditation for forty-nine days. At night, seeing the morning star rising, he became enlightened and understood the cycle of human life, i.e. the twelve causes and conditions.

Why do I talk about this morality today? Because when I first arrived in Hong Kong in 1949, the first disciple who took refuge with me was Ms. La Qua Minh. She is 81 years old this year. Yesterday morning she passed away, making me emotional. She was oppressed by circumstances all her life, but she did not surrender to adversity, patiently endured and raised her five daughters. Now her children have grown up and are relatively successful. So Ms. Guo Ming could have gone happily, or she could have been reborn in the Pure Land.

(September 4, 1983)

tieu_de: A Very Difficult Sutra to Chant
tom_tat: There is a proverb that says: "Everyone has a set of sutras in their home that is difficult to recite." When will we finish reciting this set of sutras? No one can know. When can this sutra be recited, no one knows. As long as we cultivators can…
noi_dung:
A Very Difficult Sutra to Recite

There is a proverb that says: "Everyone has a set of sutras in their home that is difficult to recite, " when will they finish reciting this set of sutras? No one can know. When can this sutra be recited, no one knows. As long as we cultivators can recite all of this sutra, we will be able to understand other sutras very easily.

Today I tell you this cause and effect because I want you to be vigilant about the issue of birth, old age, sickness and death. When encountering the above realm (i.e. the story of birth, old age, illness, death), you must think clearly, let go of everything, do not be entangled with the realm, it is best to " mindlessly face the situation, " look at everything without moving your mind, consider it normal. If someone's mind is not moved, then it is like immobility, willow willow often minh.

Everyone in life is controlled and shaken by their realm, but their realm cannot be changed. Therefore, they are confused without a goal, unable to control the Principles direction of their life, and are always confused and confused their whole life. You are born confused, die confused, once you make a mistake without realizing enlightenment, then make it again, the mistake keeps circulating in the six paths of samsara. Just like a gambler, having lost but still wanting to continue, people say: "eat less, drink less, use money to play cards" is the idea. Ordinary people always want to fight to get back the money they lost, but the more they play, the more they lose. The more they lose, the more they want to fight. In the end, they get stuck in a muddy place and can't get out. As a result, the house was destroyed and all the possessions in the house were lost (meaning that the dharma treasure of the self-nature was also lost). Yet we don't know how to return to our original source, return to the source, don't know how to reflect back, reflect on our own mind to leave the shore of ignorance and return to the shore of enlightenment, and don't know how to turn our back on the dust to merge with our awareness. People are born and then die, die and are born again, in the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death, wanting to strive to escape, but as soon as they raise their heads, they sink again, forever never escaping the sea of ​​suffering.

Monastics need to make an effort to practice, otherwise they will never leave the six paths of samsara. If you know "level save bravery" (whenever you see danger, retreat), if you know playing cards is not a good thing, but if you know it's not too late to turn back. At that time you will understand that whoever plays cards loses money, only those who do not play cards win. Just like playing chess, when you lose you win, but those who don't play chess will never lose or win. Use the above philosophy to enlighten your mind, thus understanding morality better.

Good-knowledgeable people! Reflect on birth and death, develop the mind of bodhichitta, and stop floating in the sea of ​​suffering. Anyone who doesn't want to get out of the sea of ​​suffering is stupid. If you continue to be attached to the physical world, thinking that happiness is happiness, then "this difficult-to-recite sutra" you will never be able to recite all of it. Since we have become monks, we should not recite this unreadable sutra again.

tieu_de: Cultivate a Noble Personality
tom_tat: My little friends! You should follow the example of saints and sages, learn from the example of great men, follow the example of heroes at home and abroad, from the past and...
noi_dung:
Training Noble Character

My little friends! You should follow the example of saints and sages, learn from the example of great men, follow the example of heroes at home and abroad, in the past and today, to acquire their personality, academic ethics and Buddhist karma.

Now is the time for students to study: in class, they improve their knowledge and skills, and outside of class, they practice morality and personality. When you have rich knowledge and a perfect personality, you will later make a great career and bring happiness to the whole world and humanity. Wherever you go, you need experience to progress. Don't be afraid of failure because failure is the mother of success. When you are young, you need to have the spirit of a hero, majestic and majestic, so that in the future you will become a famous speaker and an outstanding Dharma preacher.

Now is the time for students to build a solid foundation in both education and personality. The foundation of personality is even more important than the foundation of education. People who have education but do not have character will only harm the country and cause chaos for humanity. For that reason, you need to train your personality to be noble so that you can serve humanity in the future and bring benefits to Sentient Beings.

If you want to build a foundation for a solid personality, you must first learn to speak honestly and frankly, and never say lies or lies. Remember! Don't flatter, say words to make others happy, don't say words that go against your conscience, say whatever needs to be said, don't say what doesn't need to be said. You must know that: "If too many words are lost, " if you say too many words, you will make mistakes, and that "diseases come from the body, disasters come from the body,"diseases come from the mouth, disasters come from words. You must remember, be careful!

Mencius teaches us three standards for cultivating character. He said:

"Rich people are incapable of lust,

Poor and unable to move,

Majestic and invincible."

Means:

When you are rich and wealthy, you must keep the rules and not commit adultery.

When you are poor, don't change your will, that is, don't be changed by circumstances.

When we are oppressed by force, we do not submit or surrender, that is, we do not lose our reputation by profit or material things. If you have such heroic and upright character, then you can become useful people in the future.

(September 4, 1982)

tieu_de: Ten Thousand Truong High Buildings Are All Built From The Ground Up
tom_tat: My little friends! You should know that the 10,000-foot tall building is built from the ground. A tree that is one hundred feet tall also grows from inch to inch. People also grow more and more every day. When I was young, I had to make…
noi_dung:
Ten Thousand Truong High Buildings Were Built From the Ground

My little friends! You should know that the 10,000-foot tall building is built from the ground. A tree that is one hundred feet tall also grows from inch to inch. People also grow more and more every day. When you are young, you must make a wish and then move forward towards your goal. If there is no goal, no Principles, no direction, then it is like a blind person riding a blind horse, at night he can fall into a deep hole. Let's see if it's dangerous or not?

Children are like pure cloth. If dyed blue it becomes green, if dyed yellow it becomes golden. Children change depending on their educational circumstances, so people say: close to ink, it's black, close to light, it's bright. Children are conditioned by circumstances. The book Three Characters Sutra says:

Primitive humanity, inherently good nature

The nature is close, the set is distant,

Dog is not religious, nature is natural.

It means that at the beginning of human life, the nature is pure and good. Everyone's temperament is almost the same, but due to accumulated habits, one person is different from another, so if one is not educated at a young age, one's personality will change.

If you enjoy the education in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, if you can practice not fighting, not being greedy, not seeking, not seeking personal gain, not being selfish, not lying, then in the future you will definitely make great contributions to the country and society. In the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, Dharma Realm University, Virtue Cultivation High School, Duc Luong Primary School were established and all took the above six Principles as educational mottos.

Teachers of university, middle, and elementary schools! Please keep in mind the task of educating your children for the future. This is divine work. Educate students so that they become people with good and perfect personalities, with extensive education, and will not become hooligans, vagabonds, or thieves in the future, but good citizens who know how to keep order and discipline. Why is the current education system failing? It's because selfish individualism is harmful. Most people open schools to make money, so they want to have as many students as possible and destroy the noble Principles of education.

Dear teachers,

Please apply the spirit of "considering other people's children as your own" to educate them. Children are the country's resource, and also the nation's foundation. How can a country with insufficient resources and an unstable foundation become rich and strong? Please try your best!

tieu_de: Study well to perfect filial piety
tom_tat: This Avalokitesvara Seven session had many students participating. Children must clearly understand the ethics of filial piety towards their parents. When I was at home, I listened and helped my parents clean the house, sweep it clean, help my father mow the lawn,...
noi_dung:
Study well to perfect filial piety

This Avalokitesvara Seven session had many students participating. Children must clearly understand the ethics of filial piety towards their parents. When I'm at home, I obey, help my parents clean the house, sweep it clean, help my father mow the lawn, do what needs to be done. When I go to school, I have to listen to the teacher, concentrate on listening to lectures, study hard, and don't let time go to waste. One day I must know a word, one day I must learn a good sentence, that is a sign of filial piety to my parents.

Remember, in school you have to be a good student, when you come home, you have to be a good son. Not only do we have to listen to the teachings of our parents, but we have to listen to the advice of our elders. We need to be filial to our parents and respectful to our elders, because they have more experience than us and have more education than us. Therefore, you need to learn from them, consider them as examples, to have a bright future, otherwise your path will be dark and your future life will no longer have hope.

As students, you need to have clear goals, steadfast aspirations, be patient, never be shaken, and do not give up even if you encounter hundreds of thousands of difficulties. With such a spirit, only then will you be able to do great things and become great heroes. When children study, they must diligently read books, cannot waste time playing around, and must commit to studying everything necessary. Only then will we not disappoint our parents, our teachers, and the school.

You should know that this is a Buddhist school, specializing in education and teaching talented people, so that in the future, when you graduate, you will become useful people in the world. I hope that for the sake of the human world, you will strive for happiness and not let the world become degenerate. That is the hope of our school. The children here learn everything that needs to be learned honestly, meaning that even a minute of time should not be wasted, that "The mountain and the road need to be learned, learning the sea is endless, the mountain of books has a path, that path is diligence; The ocean of education is boundless, but if you use hardship as your boat, you can cross it.

You must have the spirit of patience and hard work, do not mind hardships, should not be lazy but must practice frugality, you must cherish a page or a pen, do not throw it away arbitrarily, in life you need to have rules, go to bed early at night, get up early in the morning, watch less TV, read a lot of wise books, if there is any homework in school, you must do it all when you come home, always review it, because "conscientiousness and wisdom new," only learns new knowledge by reviewing old books. Reading books once has its good qualities. Don't consider cartoon books useless.

In China, during the Eastern Han Dynasty, there was a child named Khong Dung, extremely intelligent and filial. One day, friends gave my family a basket of pears. Khong Dung's older brother chose the largest pear. At that time, Khong Dung was only four years old but knew how to be polite, so he only chose the smallest pear. His father asked:

"Why don't you take the biggest pear?"

Khong Dung replied: "Because I am young, I only eat small fruits. I will leave the big ones to my parents and brother."

Think about it, Khong Dung is only four years old, but he already knows how to be humble, love his brothers, and be filial to his parents. Such virtue is not something that every child has. His good reputation, passed down through ancient times, is known to everyone. That's why there is a saying: "Dung is four years old, he gives up pears, " means that at the age of four, Confucius knew how to give up pears.

Also in the Eastern Han Dynasty, there was a child named Hoang Huong. When he was only nine years old, his mother died. He was extremely filial to his father. In the winter, I used my body to warm my father's bed. I was afraid that my father would get cold. During the summer, she used a fan to fan her father's bed, because she was afraid of his father's heat. That was also the filial piety that the world would forever pass down, saying: " Huong is nine years old, can be gentle, " means that Hoang Huong was only nine years old and already knew how to fan her father's bed.

Those two children acted like that because their sincerity was revealed, not just a fake appearance to deceive others. Such behavior is worthy of imitation. You are all children, you need to learn from the example of these two children, how to be filial to your parents, take that as an example.

You are very lucky to be born in a rich country, have a peaceful life, and have abundant material resources. In such a privileged situation, if you do not study well, you will disappoint the hopes of your parents and teachers.

In this extremely happy country, we always need honest people, people who understand morality, understand how to love the country, and how to be an excellent citizen. If you study in a Buddhist school, you must become a teacher and an example for society in the future, leading people on the path of goodness. You must take the Six Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas as the standard: Don't fight, don't be greedy, don't seek, don't be selfish, don't seek personal gain, and don't lie. If you can truly do these six things, in the future you will become the most outstanding person in the world. I hope that you will become completely perfect people, people who can influence people to change from evil to good, to be people with great compassion, to give pleasure to Sentient Beings, and to eliminate their suffering. If so, this world will become a place of universal unity.

tieu_de: Educational Obligations of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas
tom_tat: At the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, Duc Luong Primary School, Virtue Cultivation High School and Dharma Realm University were established, all tuition-free. That is the educational obligation of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. Now I will tell…
noi_dung:
Education Obligation of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas

At the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, Duc Luong Primary School, Virtue Cultivation High School and Dharma Realm University were established, all tuition-free. That is the educational obligation of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. Now I will tell you the reason why I do not collect tuition.

My house is in the mountainous region of Song Thanh district, Northeast province. Because transportation there is very difficult, there is no school in the village, so most children are uneducated and most people in the village are illiterate. In the fall of my fifteenth year, I attended a private school and read the Four Books and the Five Classics. When I was seventeen years old, in the winter, I finished studying the Four Books and the Five Classics. My teacher explained the meaning of the books to me according to what I had learned. In total, I only studied for two and a half years.

By the age of eighteen, there were no books to read. At that time, I was at home studying medical books, roughly reading fifteen or sixteen books. Thanks to this, we can clearly understand the principle "voi queu tien van" (observe, ask questions, diagnose the pulse, listen), i.e. the four ways to examine a patient, and also know the nature "cold heat moderate " (cold, hot, warm, regulate) i.e. the four characteristics of medicine. At that time, I could also treat diseases, but I did not want to examine people, because I thought that if out of a hundred sick people I could cure ninety-nine people, if the remaining one person was not healed or if he died because he took the wrong medicine or because he treated the wrong disease, that would still be a sin. That's why I don't want to be a doctor. Furthermore, I have never valued money and until now that personality has not changed.

Also in that year, at the age of eighteen, I also read books about physiognomy, books about fortune-telling, or books about eight characters, books about math, etc. As for medicine books, books about fortune-telling, books about fortune-telling, although I was not very proficient, I still understood the meaning of it. However, I just don't want to do that job, because I don't want to make money and always think: "Richness is like flowers on the road, fame and fortune are above the dew," are all impermanent (wealth and wealth are like flowers on the roadside, fame and fortune are like dew drops on a tile).

That winter, I saw that the children in the village did not have the opportunity to study, which was pitiful, so I decided to establish a free school, without charging any tuition. At that time, there were about thirty students that I taught alone. Because the students' ages are not uniform and their understanding is also different, I have to teach according to their level. The school opens at seven o'clock in the morning, and students don't leave until six o'clock in the afternoon. During that time, there is no time to think about studying. Students work hard to study so they progress very quickly. Winter passed, the course ended and the students' performance was very good. They understand the meaning clearly and can write many words. That is the joy that I have worked hard to obtain.

Due to the above conditions, tuition is free at Duc Luong Primary School, Virtue Development High School, and Phap Gioi University. Some people are skeptical and ask if this is too stupid? Maybe I don't know the value of money? This is extremely stupid, I accept such comments. But I think that education to train talented people is the greatest happiness in life.

Now talking about Duc Luong Primary School: Principles are to educate students to become excellent talents, educate them to become honest citizens, and to become filial children, so it is called Duc Luong.

Regarding Virtue Cultivation High School, because human virtue is complete and perfect, virtue must be fostered and the cultivation of blessings and wisdom promoted. Duc Luong Primary School focuses on filial piety: The hundred virtues of filial piety are the first, among the hundred virtues, filial piety is the top priority. Virtue Cultivation High School focuses on loyalty and filial piety: loyalty to the country, filial piety to parents.

If you want to be an honest citizen who loves your country, you need to have a personality that can endure all challenges and not give up and surrender to circumstances. That's why there is a saying: "From a poor family comes filial piety, in chaos a loyal servant emerges, " from a poor family only then recognizes filial children, in a chaotic state only then comes a loyal servant. It is because they have gone through trials and tribulations that they have become such people. Those with noble personalities, those with great aspirations, those with unshakable patience, those with the talent to make great careers: these are the training goals of the Virtue Cultivation High School.

Talking about Dharma Realm University, after students at Dharma Realm School have cultivated their virtues to perfection, they can study at Dharma Realm University to become outstanding talents. We hope that boys and girls will become more outstanding than their predecessors, and in the future they can become heroes who hold their heads above the sky and their feet on the ground. You should have altruistic thoughts, others sink just as you sink, others are hungry just as you are hungry. You must have a spirit that is vast and pervades the entire emptiness of the dharma world, nothing can change your aspirations.

Currently, most schools, whether public or private, are focusing on how to make money for students, how to increase tuition every year, making people who don't have enough money just watch and lament. Because the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas wants to solve that problem, it does not charge tuition fees, but only takes the education of talented people in the world as its Principles. I hope that the students at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas are aware of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas' dedication to suffering, and have sacrificed funds to educate them to become the pillars of the nation, talented people to propagate the Dharma. You should not ignore the hard work of the teachers at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, you must study hard. There is a saying: "When using books, there is no need to hate, the lack of experience is too difficult, " means that when it is time to use books, you will regret that you lack knowledge, without experiencing it, you will not know how difficult it is. If you don't study hard now, when the time comes when you need to use your knowledge in the future, you will regret it immensely. That's what I need to tell you today.

(September 19, 1983)

noi_dung:
Children Are the Pillars of the Country

Dear little friends! Please sit upright, quietly listen to what I want to say today. You are young trees that grow taller and taller every day. In the future, you will be a pillar for our country. You need to create a great and glorious career, bring peace to the world, bring happiness to humanity. You were born in America and you have to make this country well-managed, so that there will be no more wars in the country, there will be eternal peace, and for the whole world, everywhere and every country, there will be peace, that is your mission.

Now, let's lay a solid foundation for saving the country and people in the future. First, you must learn to be a good person, that is, you should follow the example of good people and learn, do not learn from bad people. What is a good person? That is, at home, be filial to your parents. When you go to school, you respect your master and teachers. In society, you serve the people. When you work in the government, you always seek happiness for the people. That is the standard of a good person. What is a bad person? Bad people are selfish, only seek their own benefits, and are ungrateful. Good people who rule the country will make the country rich and strong, without war. If bad people rule the country, they will lose the country.

They are pioneers because they learn how to be filial to their parents and how to serve others. In the future, you will bring peace to this country, bring all the murderous weapons and destroy them: "The horse will be released from the south of the mountain, the swords and spears will go into the warehouse, " means releasing the war horses to the mountain to no longer be used, and putting the swords and spears in the warehouse, no longer needed. It is your responsibility to neutralize the atmosphere of war in this world, so that everyone can live in peace, have enough food and clothing. Only then can this world become "The Universal World".

(August 20, 1983)

tieu_de: What is Dignity, What is Establishment

noi_dung:
What is Don Pham, What is Establishment

Little children! Do you want to fulfill your responsibility of saving the world, saving people, saving lives, saving people? First, you must encourage the Chapter to establish virtue. What is a finished product? Don means good-natured. Chapter is Chapter manner, which means that you must learn how to enrich knowledge, Chapter manner to be noble, don't smoke, don't drink alcohol, don't smoke poker, don't gamble and drink, and don't do bad deeds. We should not learn from the unintellectual people of the past. They did not fulfill their responsibilities to the country, they did not fulfill their obligations to society, they were always arbitrary and refused to keep their own rules, becoming people who only harmed others. They are what we call Asuras in the human world. They only know how to fight but do not know peace. Such evil people only become people who are harmful to the nation.

You are now like young trees that are slowly blooming, so you must always pay attention to cutting off useless branches, so that the tree can grow straight up, and in the future become a huge tree that can be used as building material. That "Ten years to grow trees, a hundred years to grow people." You are currently in the time of studying, so you should not be infected with bad habits. Remember! You must nurture your Chapter in a noble manner, maintaining integrity and purity. If so, then they will become world leaders in the future.

What is establishing virtue? Establish means to establish or establish. Virtue is virtue, which means establishing virtue for oneself, that is, being filial to one's parents, because "The hundred virtues of filial piety are the first," among the hundred virtues, filial piety is the first. If you are not filial to your parents, even if you bow to Buddha every day, it will not be of any benefit. Children need to pay close attention to this point.

As your virtue grows more and more every day, your foundation as a human being becomes more and more solid every day. When you need to speak, you should say reasonable words, true to the truth, and should not say unreasonable or improper words. In short, you should make an effort to study, so that in the future you will become a useful person for society, and not be a bad person in the world. That is what I expect from you.

Money Can Harm Your Life

If for the above purpose we do not use any tricks, we will only create more karma.
