We in this world need to help miserable people, save them from burning water. "Doing good deeds is the highest joy,"doing good deeds is the highest joy, because helping others is the basis of happiness.

(September 22, 1983)

tieu_de: Creating a Solid Foundation
tom_tat: The educational principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas are to first build a solid personality foundation, so that everyone in elementary school, middle school, and university knows how to be respectful, honest, and filial...
noi_dung:
Creating a Solid Foundation

The educational principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas are to first build a solid foundation of character, so that everyone in elementary school, middle school, and university knows how to be respectful, filial, and compassionate. That means we must pay attention to the spirit of education. Help students have a solid foundation as human beings so that in the future, whatever they do in the world, they will do it according to ethical thinking. If so, then you can be a standard for others to imitate, or an example for others to follow, so that everyone can look at you and learn. Gradually, society's bad customs and habits will be improved, turning into a society where the house does not need to be locked at night, and objects falling on the street no one needs to pick up.

Why is this society not good? Because no one has a solid human foundation. That's why, being spoiled by wealth, beauty, fame, food, drink, and sleep, the five desires are like gusts of wind pulling in all four directions, making everyone confused and confused, only knowing how to seek pleasure and happiness, but not knowing how to be filial or faithful at all? Because they do not know the principles of benevolence, decency, wisdom, and faith, they make the world full of dark miasma and no longer have any system.

The education system at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas teaches students to have a solid foundation as a human being, from which they can mention other virtues. I am like a tamping tree, specializing in tamping the soil so that the moral foundation of the children is solid, so that they can become talented people in the future. That is my purpose.

Little friends! Don't underestimate it! You are the future owners of the country. When students go to class to study, in addition to listening to the teachers' teachings, they also have to practice how to lecture. Once you have experience in preaching, you are no longer afraid. In the future, you will be talented people who can preach the Dharma and have unhindered eloquence.

Teachers, professors! Please endure a little more suffering to educate these young men, train them to become wise people, talented people, people who boldly do it when they see a righteous cause, teach them to be willing to devote themselves to serving public affairs, protecting the law, and becoming excellent citizens. Please understand that if you want to build world peace, you must start with education. When the educational foundation is firmly established, only then can the country be prosperous and strong, and the world can be at peace. Currently, because the educational fundamentals of many countries are not solid, they create young people who do not know how to maintain rules, have enough to eat and have nothing to do, and then become romantic delinquents.

I dare say that the students who receive education at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, whether they are university students, or students in high school or elementary school, all know how to keep the rules, know their duties as humans, and know how to cultivate their virtues. I hope you take that as your motto and strive to study to become useful people for the country.

tieu_de: Confucius - Great Educator
tom_tat: During the Spring-Autumn Warring States period in China, a great saint was born, named Confucius. He spent his life traveling around the world to promote the doctrine of humanity, morality, filial piety and loyalty, but was not welcomed by anyone...
noi_dung:
Confucius - Great Educator

During the Spring-Autumn Warring States period in China, a great saint was born, named Confucius. He traveled throughout his life to promote the doctrine of humanity, morality, filial piety and loyalty, but no one welcomed him and everywhere rejected him. Although He encountered such unsatisfactory circumstances, He still did not change the Principles of education, He still faithfully promoted universalism.

Confucius was a great educator. He proposed a popular education accessible to everyone. He had the spirit of "teaching without being boring, studying without tiring." He ​​did not compose, only copied the stories of the past. He believed in what the saints said in the past, then put it into practice. At the end of his life, he published five books: Poetry, Letters, Translations, Rites, Spring and Autumn, that is, the Five Classics.

Confucius had three thousand students. He is knowledgeable about rituals, music, radio, music, letters, and numbers, called the six arts. His disciples had seventy-two people who were also proficient in the six arts. Ceremony means ceremonies and rituals related to marriage, burial, or worship. Music means music. Shooting means archery. Ngu means to take off the horse and drive the chariot. Letter means record, history. Numbers are algorithms. Each subject must be completely mastered to be considered a complete person.

Confucius's educational motto is to take people as the center and take oneself as an example. His disciples have four excellent grades:

1. Outstanding in virtue, there are Nhan Hoi and Man Tu Khiem.

Excellent in language and debate include Tu Ha and Te Nga.

Outstanding in politics include Mr. Tu Lo and Mr. Nhiem Huu.

Outstanding in literature include Tzu Ha and Tzu Du.

When Confucius passed away, Confucianism divided into two sects. Zeng Tu advocated propagating the Tao, and Mencius represented this sect, becoming the orthodox sect. Tu Ha advocated transmitting the Sutras, and Sun Tzu was the representative of this sect. The Sutra tradition flourished during the three dynasties of Han, Tang, and Qing. The Taoist sect flourished during the Song, Yuan, and Ming dynasties.

All things in the world are interrelated, just like in China, the three religions of Confucianism, Buddhism, and Taoism all support each other. Confucianism is like the elementary level, that is, elementary school, Taoism is like the middle school level, and Buddhism is like the university level. The ethics of these three religions are all related, but people in elementary school do not know the level of high school, but people in college know the level and lessons of middle school or elementary school.

Confucianism teaches human ethics, such as cultivating a good personality. Half of Taoism focuses on cultivating moral character, while the other half focuses on cultivating the world. Therefore, Taoist monks do not shave their heads or beards, and are no different from lay people. They only wear the clothes of ancient hermits. In Buddhism, you must shave your beard and hair, wear colorful robes, do not pay attention to appearance, but the robe never leaves the body and must show the appearance of a Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī. Buddhism is about practicing dharma beyond the world, is it breaking away from worldly dharma and creating a separate Buddha dharma? That's not it. Just need to perceive worldly dharma clearly, not be confused by it, that is Buddha dharma.

There are people who advocate the unity of the three religions (ie Taoism,

Confucianism and Buddhism combine into one), so there is a saying:

Pink flowers, white flowers, green leaves,

Three sects originally came from one family.

(Rose, white stem, green leaves,

Those three religions belong to the same family.)

That is a manifestation of morality. The basis of Buddhism, to develop a belief in mind, is Confucianism, so it is necessary to read books, understand the meaning, first understand what is the basis of being human, then follow the Dharma to practice: Return to the original nature, non-duality, means have many doors. Meaning: returning to the source is emptiness, but the means have many entrances. People who study Buddhism need to understand this principle thoroughly.

(September 25, 1983)

The Way of the "University Level"

The religion of the "University level" takes three platforms and eight articles as Principles. What are the three platforms? That means being virtuous, friendly to the people, and just being good. Minh virtue means that after we purify ourselves and illuminate our own light and nature, we later teach others to illuminate and purify their own light and nature. Being close to the people means making everyone know the righteous path, how to become people who understand morality. Only with good will is everyone reaching the ultimate point of goodness.

What are the eight articles, eight terms, or eight conditions? That is, the way of things, wisdom, right mind, sincerity, self-cultivation, family discipline, government, and peace in the world.

What is the way of object? That is, studying the nature of all things in heaven and earth.

What is intelligence? It is to apply wisdom, meticulously study the style of all things to know the extreme.

What is right mind? That is, the virtuous mind is the master of one's body.

Sincerity means having sincere intentions.

Self-cultivation means changing and practicing to become a good and virtuous person.

Those are five things that belong to the learning of the body and mind.

Qi Gia means governing one's own family.

To govern means to manage and lead one's country.

To pacify the world means to make the world peaceful.

These three things belong to the subject of politics.

The above is the doctrine of Confucius and also the very basic ideal of Confucian ethics. Today I only briefly explain the three platforms and eight articles in the book "University, " I will explain more clearly to you in the future.

tieu_de: Summary of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua
tom_tat: Venerable Master Hsuan Hua's family name is Bach, his real name is An Tu, his nickname is Do Luan. He is from Song Thanh district, Song Giang province in Northeast China, that is, Manchu
noi_dung:
Summary of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua

Venerable Master Hsuan Hua's family name is Bach, his real name is An Tu, his nickname is Do Luan. He is from Songcheng district, Songjiang province in Northeast China, that is, Manchuria.

His father's name was Phu Hai, specializing in farming. Her mother, surnamed Ho, gave birth to a total of eight children, five boys and three girls; and He is the youngest.

Mrs. Ho adopted a vegetarian diet and recited Buddha's name without interruption. One night, the lady had a dream and saw Amitabha Buddha appearing incarnate, emitting great light, illuminating the world, shaking heaven and earth. Startled awake, the lady smelled a wonderful scent throughout the room, and then gave birth to Him.

As soon as he was born, he cried continuously for three days and nights without stopping.

It is because of grief for the suffering of this Saha world.

He lives in a very small village with few houses. Therefore, until the age of eleven, he had never seen a dead person. One day, he and his friends in the village went on a field trip. Suddenly he saw a baby, mouth closed, eyes closed, lying bundled up in the straw on the sidelines. He called but the child did not respond. When he touched it, there was no breath. He was extremely confused so he asked his friends. Someone who understood immediately said: "The baby is dead!" But he was extremely surprised, not understanding what death was. Returning home, he immediately asked his mother, who taught: "Every human being, everyone must die. Some people die of old age, some die of illness, and some die of accidents. Regardless of whether one is rich or poor, whether one is a scholar, a farmer, a worker, a merchant, or a mandarin, everyone must eventually die."

He asked again: "If that's true, is there any way to escape death?"At that time, there was a guest in the house who had practiced the Way in the past. He answered and said: "Only by cultivating the Way, enlightening one's own mind, and fully understanding one's own nature can one end birth and death, transcend samsara, attain perfect Enlightenment, and attain Infertility."

Although he was still young at that time, he was deeply enlightened by what the guest said, so he decided to become a monk and practice the Way.

When he discussed the matter of becoming a monk with his mother, she taught: "Becoming a monk is a very good thing, but it is not an easy thing to do. We need to have good roots, great aspiration power, and need to develop great Bodhi mind to be able to achieve the Supreme Path. Now that you have that kind of heart, I wholeheartedly agree, it's really in line with that old dream. Now I am old, my days are short, my brothers and sisters are all independent. Children should stay to take care of their parents; When I die, you will become a monk, it will not be too late."

He obeyed his parents, and then every day he followed his mother to bow to Buddha. After bowing to Buddha, he bowed to his parents.

Day after day, as winter fades and spring comes, he respectfully takes care of his parents as if he were Buddha. Soon his reputation for filial piety spread throughout the four directions, at that time everyone called him Bach Hieu Tu (filial son of the Bach family).

When he was 19 years old, his mother passed away; At that time, he said goodbye to his relatives and went to the temple to bow to the Venerable Thuong Tri as his teacher and took refuge, officially becoming a monk and receiving ordination. After that, he returned to his mother's grave to pay filial piety for three years. During that time, he lived in a small thatched hut, meditating every day, reading Mahayana sutras and chanting the name of Amitabha Buddha. Many times he sat in meditation and then entered concentration, continuously for many weeks without leaving the meditation bed.

One night, people in a nearby village were frightened to see his thatched hut burning with red fire. The red fire glowed straight up in the air and the thatched hut was as bright as day. Many people ran to the grave, shouting: "Hieu Tu's house is on fire!" Hundreds of people in the village gathered to put out ladles and buckets to put out the fire. However, when they arrived, they only saw a peaceful thatched hut, no fire burning and He was still at peace and quiet in Meditation!

One time he was meditating when suddenly a guest came to visit. That guest, surprisingly, was the Sixth Patriarch Huineng! The Patriarch taught him that in the future he would go to America to save sentient beings, that in the West he would meet many predestined people who could propagate Buddha Dharma and that he would save boundless Sentient Beings. It was not until the Patriarch said goodbye and turned away that he woke up and remembered that Huineng was originally from the Tang Dynasty, 1,200 years ago. After World War II, he traveled everywhere. Finally, after traveling more than three thousand miles, he arrived at Nam Hoa Pagoda and paid homage to the Great Wise One of that time, Elder Venerable Hu Van. The Venerable was 109 years old at that time; As soon as he saw Him, the Venerable immediately recognized His enlightenment. At that time, the Venerable said: "Like this, like like!"; and He also replied: "As it is, as it is!"

At that time, Old Venerable Hu Van confirmed his attainment, and he officially became the ninth Patriarch of the Quy Ngoc dharma lineage.

After that, the Venerable Master taught him to stay at the temple and take on the position of Head of the Institute of Precepts of Nam Hoa Temple.

In 1950, he left the temple and left for Hong Kong. Here, He lives in an isolated cave, without visiting dust or worldly things. Soon, countless monks from Mainland China came to Hong Kong as refugees, and they needed His help. Finally, according to fate, he left the cave, established a lecture hall and two pagodas, and helped build many other Bodhimandas.

During his twelve years in Hong Kong, he was a shining example of asceticism, diligence in cultivating the Way, and forgetting himself for the sake of Buddha Dharma. He has influenced countless good men and women, causing them to develop Bodhi minds, take refuge in the Three Jewels, and support Buddha Dharma.

In 1962, he came to San Francisco, USA. Here, in a small warehouse, he persistently practiced in silence, waiting for the opportunity to propagate the Dharma to ripen. At that time, he called himself "Tom Trung Tang" (the monk in the grave), or Hoat Tu Nhan (the one who died but is still alive). Buddhists who understand his true practice are very moved and respectfully support and make offerings to him.

In 1968, he knew the opportunity had come; He said: "A flower will bloom with five petals." That summer, he presided over a Dharma conference teaching the Shurangama Sutra for 96 days. When the Dharma Conference ended, sure enough, the first five Americans asked to become monks with him.

From then on, he continued to preside over many other Dharma conferences, explaining the Mind

Sutra, Ksitigarbha Sutra, Lotus Sutra, Dharma Jewel Platform Sutra, etc.

In 1971, he preached the supreme sutra of Mahayana, which is the Avatamsaka Sutra.

Along with preaching the Sutras and preaching the Dharma, he also did countless other meritorious deeds to save sentient beings. In 1976, he founded the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, a base to propagate Buddhism in the United States. In the Holy City, he built the Tung Lam regime, trained monks and nuns, studied them, and created excellent conditions for true practice.

I pray that I will divide countless souls and enter the minds of Sentient Beings who do not believe in the Buddha Dharma, causing them to abandon evil, turn to goodness, repent and correct themselves, take refuge in the Three Jewels, and finally become Buddhas.

muscle.
